patterns: take after someone more than + person
Which parent do you take after?

usage.object: The object normally follows after: She takes after her mother.
usage.inseparability: The expression is inseparable; do not say take her mother after.
usage.family: It most commonly describes resemblance to an older family member in appearance, personality, behavior, or ability.
usage.trait: Use in to specify the area of resemblance: He takes after his father in temperament.
usage.appearance: Take after may include physical resemblance, but it can equally describe character, habits, talents, or interests.
usage.contrast: Look like mainly concerns appearance, whereas take after commonly suggests a broader or inherited family resemblance.

ja: 外見が親・祖父母などの年長の家族に似ている
性格・気質が家族の誰かに似ている
才能・能力・関心などを家族から受け継いでいるように見える
話し方・行動・習慣などが年長の親族と共通している
複数の親族を比較して、特定の人により強く似ている
en: to resemble a parent, grandparent, or other older relative in appearance
to have a personality or temperament similar to that of a family member
to appear to inherit a relative’s talent, ability, or interests
to share an older relative’s manner of speaking, behavior, or habits
to resemble one particular relative more strongly than another

nuance.ja: take after は、主として子どもや若い世代が親・祖父母などの年長の親族に似ていることを表す。外見だけでなく、性格・才能・癖・職業的関心などにも使える。She takes after her mother. だけでは、具体的に何が似ているかは文脈で判断する。外見に限定するなら look like、より一般的・形式的に類似を述べるなら resemble が使える。通常、年下の人物を基準にして年長者との類似を述べるため、親が子どもに似ているという意味で The mother takes after her daughter. とするのは不自然である。
nuance.en: Take after primarily describes a younger person’s resemblance to a parent, grandparent, or other older relative. The resemblance may concern appearance, personality, talent, habits, or professional interests. In She takes after her mother, context determines the particular shared quality. Look like is more specifically concerned with physical appearance, while resemble is a more general and somewhat more formal alternative. Because the expression normally presents the older relative as the source or model of the trait, The mother takes after her daughter sounds unnatural if it merely means that the mother resembles the daughter.

ja: take after：外見・性格・才能などが親や年長の親族に似ている。
look like：人・物の外見が別の人・物に似ている。
resemble：外見・性質・構造などが似ている。より一般的・形式的。
be like：性格・行動・状況などが似ていることを広く表す。
inherit：遺伝的特徴・財産・権利などを親や前任者から受け継ぐ。
get something from someone：特徴・能力などを人から受け継いだと口語的に述べる。
run in the family：特徴・能力・病気などが家系の複数人に共通している。
follow in someone’s footsteps：年長者と同じ職業・生き方・行動を選ぶ。
en: take after means resembling a parent or older relative in appearance, personality, talent, or behavior.
look like means having a physical appearance similar to that of another person or thing.
resemble generally and somewhat formally describes similarity in appearance, nature, or structure.
be like broadly expresses similarity in personality, behavior, or circumstances.
inherit means receiving a genetic trait, property, right, or position from a parent or predecessor.
get something from someone informally attributes a personal quality or ability to a family member.
run in the family means that a characteristic, ability, or illness occurs in several members of a family.
follow in someone’s footsteps means choosing the same profession, lifestyle, or course of action as an older person.

etymology.ja: take は古ノルド語 taka「つかむ、取る」に由来し、after は古英語 æfter「後に、後を追って」にさかのぼる。take after はもともと、人や物の後を追う、追跡するという意味でも使われた。そこから、年長者の後をたどるように、その外見・性格・行動様式を受け継ぐという比喩的意味が発達した。現代英語では、親族への類似を表す用法が中心である。
etymology.en: Take derives from Old Norse taka, to grasp or take, while after comes from Old English æfter, behind or following. Take after was formerly used for pursuing or following someone. From the idea of following an older person developed the figurative sense of continuing or reproducing that person’s appearance, character, or behavior. In modern English, resemblance to a parent or other older relative is its principal meaning.

note.ja: 親族に限らず、人・物が外見・性質・構造などの点で似ていることを表す。
note.en: To be similar to a person or thing in appearance, character, or structure, without being limited to relatives.

note.ja: 主として顔・体格などの外見上の類似を日常的に表す。
note.en: An everyday expression mainly describing similarity in facial features, build, or other aspects of appearance.

note.ja: 人の性格・態度・行動などが別の人に似ていることを広く表す。
note.en: A broad expression for being similar to another person in personality, attitude, or behavior.

note.ja: 身体的特徴・性格傾向・能力などを親から遺伝的または比喩的に受け継ぐ。
note.en: To receive a physical trait, tendency, or ability genetically or figuratively from a parent.

note.ja: 特にアメリカ英語で、外見が家族の誰かに似ていることを表す。
note.en: Especially in American English, to resemble a particular family member in appearance.

ja: take after one’s mother — 母親に似ている
take after one’s father — 父親に似ている
take after one’s grandmother — 祖母に似ている
take after both parents — 両親のどちらにも似ている
take after someone physically — 身体的特徴が人に似ている
take after someone in appearance — 外見が人に似ている
take after someone in personality — 性格が人に似ている
take after someone in temperament — 気質が人に似ている
take after someone musically — 音楽的才能が人に似ている

seem to take after someone — 人に似ているように見える
take after one parent more than the other — もう一方より一方の親に似ている

take after one’s father
take after one’s grandmother
take after both parents
take after someone physically
take after someone in appearance
take after someone in personality
take after someone in temperament
take after someone musically

ja: She takes after her mother in both appearance and personality. — 彼女は外見も性格も母親に似ている。
Which side of the family do you take after? — あなたは父方と母方のどちらの家族に似ていますか。
He looks like his father, but he takes after his mother in temperament. — 彼は外見は父親似だが、気質は母親似だ。
All three children take after their grandfather musically. — 三人の子どもは全員、音楽的な才能が祖父に似ている。
She became a patent attorney like her father, although she says she takes after her mother in her careful attention to language. — 彼女は父親と同じく弁理士になったが、言葉への細やかな注意力は母親譲りだという。
en: She takes after her mother in both appearance and personality.
Which side of the family do you take after?
He looks like his father, but he takes after his mother in temperament.
All three children take after their grandfather musically.
She became a patent attorney like her father, although she says she takes after her mother in her careful attention to language.

grammar.countability: countable as a noun

usage.skin: A blemish commonly means a small mark, spot, discoloration, or pimple affecting the appearance of the skin.
usage.surface: It can refer to a small flaw or mark on an object’s otherwise smooth or attractive surface.
usage.figurative: A blemish on a reputation or record is an event or fault that damages an otherwise favorable image.
usage.verb: As a verb, blemish means spoiling appearance, quality, reputation, or an otherwise good record.
usage.severity: The word usually suggests a localized imperfection rather than complete destruction or fundamental failure.
usage.medical_caution: Blemish is a general descriptive word and is not a precise medical diagnosis for a skin condition.

ja: 皮膚に生じた小さな吹き出物・しみ・変色などの外見上の欠点
物の表面にある小さな傷・斑点・汚れ
完全性・美しさ・品質を損なう小さな欠陥
経歴・評判・実績を傷つける失敗・不名誉
動詞として、外見・品質・評判などに傷をつける
en: a small pimple, mark, spot, or discoloration affecting the appearance of the skin
a minor scratch, stain, spot, or flaw on the surface of an object
a small imperfection that reduces beauty, quality, or completeness
a fault, failure, or disgrace damaging an otherwise favorable record or reputation
as a verb, to spoil the appearance, quality, reputation, or record of someone or something

nuance.ja: blemish は、全体を使用不能にする重大な欠陥というより、概して良好な外見・品質・評判の一部を損なう局所的な傷や欠点を表す。肌については吹き出物・しみ・赤みなどを広く指すが、医学的な診断名ではない。a blemish on his record は、それ以外は良好な経歴に残った一つの汚点という意味である。flaw は構造・論理・性格などの内部的欠陥にも広く使え、defect は製品や機能上の欠陥をより客観的・技術的に表す。blemish は特に外観や評判を「きれいでないものにする」という評価を帯びる。
nuance.en: A blemish is usually a localized imperfection affecting something otherwise attractive, successful, or of good quality, rather than a defect that makes the whole item unusable. On skin, it broadly includes pimples, marks, spots, and discoloration but is not a medical diagnosis. A blemish on his record means a particular fault or failure damaging an otherwise favorable history. Flaw more broadly includes internal weaknesses in reasoning, design, or character, while defect is a more objective or technical term for a problem in a product or function. Blemish particularly suggests spoiling a clean appearance or favorable reputation.

ja: blemish：肌・表面・評判などの美しさや完全性を損なう、局所的な傷・欠点・汚点。
flaw：物・設計・論理・性格などにある不完全な点や弱点。
defect：製品・構造・機能などが基準どおりでない客観的・技術的な欠陥。
stain：液体などによる落ちにくい汚れ。または評判に残る汚点。
scar：傷が治癒した後に残る痕。または過去の苦痛が残した心理的影響。
mark：表面に見える線・点・跡を広く表す中立的な語。
imperfection：完全・理想的でない部分を広く表す。
blot：インクなどのしみ、または名誉・経歴を著しく損なう汚点。
en: a blemish is a localized mark or fault spoiling otherwise good skin, appearance, quality, or reputation.
a flaw is an imperfection or weakness in an object, design, argument, or character.
a defect is an objective or technical failure of a product, structure, or function to meet a standard.
a stain is a persistent discolored mark or figuratively a lasting mark on a reputation.
a scar is a mark left after a wound heals or a lasting psychological effect of past suffering.
a mark is a broad and neutral term for a visible line, spot, or trace on a surface.
an imperfection is any feature preventing something from being completely perfect or ideal.
a blot is an ink-like mark or a serious figurative stain on someone’s honor or record.

etymology.ja: blemish は古フランス語 blemir、blêmir「青ざめさせる、傷つける、色を損なう」に由来すると考えられている。もとは身体や表面の色・外見を悪化させることを表し、そこから美しさや完全性を損なう傷・しみ・欠点という名詞の意味が発達した。さらに、外見上の汚点を評判・名誉・経歴上の失敗になぞらえる比喩的用法が生まれた。
etymology.en: Blemish is generally traced to Old French blemir or blêmir, meaning to make pale, injure, or spoil the color of something. It initially concerned damage to bodily or surface appearance. From this developed the noun sense of a mark, spot, or imperfection reducing beauty or completeness. Physical discoloration was then metaphorically extended to a fault or disgrace damaging a person’s reputation, honor, or record.

note.ja: 外観だけでなく、設計・推論・性格・計画などにある不完全な点や弱点を広く表す。
note.en: A broad term for an imperfection or weakness in appearance, design, reasoning, character, or planning.

note.ja: 物・人・制度などが完全または理想的でない原因となる部分。
note.en: A feature or condition preventing a person, object, or system from being completely perfect or ideal.

note.ja: 皮膚・布・物の表面などに残る線・点・変色を中立的に表す。
note.en: A neutral word for a visible line, spot, discoloration, or trace on skin, fabric, or another surface.

note.ja: 表面に染み込んだ汚れ、または人の名誉・評判に残る不名誉な汚点。
note.en: A discolored mark absorbed into a surface or a figurative disgrace remaining on someone’s reputation.

note.ja: 製品・材料・構造・機能などが要求される基準を満たさない欠陥。
note.en: A fault causing a product, material, structure, or function to fail to satisfy a required standard.

a facial blemish — 顔の肌にある傷・吹き出物
a minor blemish — 小さな欠点・傷

a facial blemish

ja: The cream is designed to reduce the appearance of minor skin blemishes. — そのクリームは、肌の小さな吹き出物やしみを目立たなくするためのものだ。
The table was sold at a discount because of a small surface blemish. — そのテーブルは表面に小さな傷があったため、割引価格で販売された。
The scandal left a permanent blemish on his otherwise impressive career. — その不祥事は、それ以外は立派だった彼の経歴に消えない汚点を残した。
One unsuccessful project should not blemish the reputation of the entire team. — 一件の失敗したプロジェクトによって、チーム全体の評判が傷つけられるべきではない。
A minor drafting blemish may be harmless, but an ambiguous claim limitation can materially affect the scope of a patent. — 些細な起草上の不備なら無害なこともあるが、曖昧な請求項の限定は特許の範囲に重大な影響を与え得る。
en: The cream is designed to reduce the appearance of minor skin blemishes.
The table was sold at a discount because of a small surface blemish.
The scandal left a permanent blemish on his otherwise impressive career.
One unsuccessful project should not blemish the reputation of the entire team.
A minor drafting blemish may be harmless, but an ambiguous claim limitation can materially affect the scope of a patent.

grammar.countability: normally uncountable
patterns: the competitiveness of + company / industry / economy

usage.uncountable: Competitiveness is normally uncountable: improve competitiveness, not improve a competitiveness.
usage.business: For a company or product, it means the ability to compete successfully in price, quality, innovation, service, or other relevant factors.
usage.economy: For an economy or country, it may refer to productivity, institutional conditions, costs, innovation, trade performance, and the capacity to support successful businesses.
usage.personality: For an individual, competitiveness can mean a strong desire to win or perform better than others.
usage.price: Price competitiveness specifically concerns whether a price is attractive relative to competing offers.
usage.evaluation: Competitiveness is generally positive in business contexts, but excessive personal competitiveness may be criticized.

ja: 企業・製品・産業などが市場で競争し成功する能力、競争力
価格・品質・技術・サービスなどの面で競合より優位に立てる程度
国・地域の企業が国内外の市場で価値を生み出し続ける能力
生産性・効率性・革新性などによって競争上の地位を維持する力
人が他者に勝ち、よりよい成果を上げようとする競争心
en: the ability of a company, product, or industry to compete successfully in a market
the degree to which an offer can outperform rivals in price, quality, technology, or service
the capacity of a country or region to support businesses that create value in domestic and international markets
the ability to maintain a competitive position through productivity, efficiency, and innovation
for a person, a strong desire to win or perform better than others

nuance.ja: competitiveness は、競争が存在すること自体を表す competition ではなく、その競争の中で成功できる能力・強さを表す。企業の competitiveness は低価格だけでなく、品質、ブランド、技術、供給力、顧客サービスなど複数の要因から成る。cost competitiveness は生産・運営コストの低さ、price competitiveness は顧客に提示する価格の魅力に焦点を置く。国の competitiveness は単純な順位ではなく、生産性、制度、インフラ、技能、革新力などを含む複雑な概念であり、評価指標によって結果が異なる。人について使う場合は「負けず嫌い・競争心」を表し、程度によって肯定的にも否定的にもなる。
nuance.en: Competitiveness does not mean the existence of competition itself; it means the ability or strength to succeed within that competition. A company’s competitiveness may depend on quality, brand recognition, technology, supply capacity, customer service, and price. Cost competitiveness focuses on keeping production or operating costs relatively low, whereas price competitiveness concerns the attractiveness of the price offered to customers. National competitiveness is a complex concept involving productivity, institutions, infrastructure, skills, and innovation, and rankings can differ according to the chosen indicators. Applied to a person, competitiveness means a desire to outperform others and may be praised or criticized depending on its intensity.

ja: competitiveness：市場・競争の中で他者と競い、成功する能力・競争力。
competition：複数の者が顧客・利益・賞などをめぐって競う状況・活動。
competitive advantage：競合より有利な地位をもたらす具体的な強み・条件。
competitive edge：競合よりわずかに優位に立たせる特徴。比較的口語的。
productivity：投入した労働・資本などに対して、どれだけ多くの成果を生み出すか。
efficiency：時間・費用・資源の無駄を抑えて成果を得る能力。
profitability：企業・事業が利益を生み出す能力・程度。
competitiveness of a person：人が他者に勝ち、優れた成果を出そうとする競争心。
en: competitiveness is the ability to compete successfully against others in a market or contest.
competition is the situation or activity in which multiple parties contend for customers, profit, prizes, or advantage.
a competitive advantage is a particular strength or condition placing a business ahead of its rivals.
a competitive edge is a relatively informal term for a feature providing a slight advantage over competitors.
productivity is the amount of output produced relative to labor, capital, or other inputs.
efficiency is the ability to achieve results while minimizing wasted time, money, or resources.
profitability is the ability or degree to which a company or activity generates profit.
personal competitiveness is a person’s desire to win or outperform others.

etymology.ja: competitiveness は competitive に状態・性質を表す接尾辞 -ness を加えた語である。competitive は compete に由来し、compete はラテン語 competere「ともに求める、同じものを目指す」から英語に入った。competere は com-「ともに」と petere「求める、目指す」から成る。複数の者が同じ目的・市場・賞を求めるという発想から competition、competitive、competitor が生まれ、competitiveness はその競争で成功できる性質・能力を表すようになった。
etymology.en: Competitiveness was formed from competitive and the quality-forming suffix -ness. Competitive derives from compete, which came from Latin competere, to seek together or strive for the same object. Competere consists of com-, together, and petere, to seek or aim at. The idea of multiple parties pursuing the same market, goal, or prize produced competition, competitor, and competitive. Competitiveness consequently denotes the quality or ability that enables a party to compete successfully.

note.ja: 企業・製品・産業が競合との比較で持つ強さを、直接的に表す。
note.en: A direct expression for the strength of a company, product, or industry relative to its rivals.

note.ja: 価格・技術・ブランドなど、競合より有利な地位を与える具体的な要因。
note.en: A specific factor such as price, technology, or brand strength that provides superiority over rivals.

note.ja: 製品・企業・人を競合より有利にする特徴やわずかな優位性。
note.en: A feature or slight advantage enabling a product, company, or person to outperform competitors.

note.ja: 市場における企業・製品の地位、影響力、販売能力などの強さ。
note.en: The strength of a company’s or product’s position, influence, and sales capacity in a market.

note.ja: 他社・他国・他者との競争で成果を上げる能力を平易に表す。
note.en: A plain expression for the capacity to succeed in competition against other companies, countries, or individuals.

ja: The company invested in automation to improve its competitiveness. — その会社は競争力を高めるため、自動化に投資した。
High transportation costs have weakened the region’s price competitiveness. — 高い輸送費が、その地域の価格競争力を弱めている。
Innovation is essential to maintaining competitiveness in a rapidly changing market. — 急速に変化する市場で競争力を維持するには、革新が不可欠である。
Her competitiveness motivates her to train harder than the other players. — 彼女の競争心は、他の選手より熱心に練習する動機になっている。

A well-managed patent portfolio can strengthen a company’s competitiveness by protecting technology that distinguishes its products from those of its rivals. — 適切に管理された特許ポートフォリオは、製品を競合品から差別化する技術を保護することで、企業の競争力を強化し得る。
en: The company invested in automation to improve its competitiveness.
High transportation costs have weakened the region’s price competitiveness.
Innovation is essential to maintaining competitiveness in a rapidly changing market.
Her competitiveness motivates her to train harder than the other players.
A well-managed patent portfolio can strengthen a company’s competitiveness by protecting technology that distinguishes its products from those of its rivals.

grammar.countability: normally uncountable
patterns: the profitability of + company / product / project

usage.uncountable: Profitability is normally uncountable: improve profitability, not improve a profitability.
usage.meaning: It describes the ability or degree to which a business, product, investment, or activity generates profit relative to relevant costs or resources.
usage.profit: Profit is the amount remaining after costs, whereas profitability concerns the capacity, rate, or efficiency of generating that profit.
usage.measurement: Profitability may be assessed using different measures, including margins and returns on assets, equity, or invested capital.
usage.time: A business may be profitable during one period without possessing sustainable long-term profitability.
usage.register: The word is standard in business, accounting, finance, investment, and economic analysis.

ja: 企業・製品・事業などが利益を生み出す能力、収益性
売上げに対してどの程度効率的に利益を得ているか
投資した資本・資産に対して利益を生み出す程度
費用を上回る収益を継続的に確保できる性質
事業・市場・顧客などが利益面でどれほど魅力的か
en: the ability of a company, product, or activity to generate profit
the degree to which profit is earned efficiently relative to sales
the amount of profit generated in relation to invested capital or assets
the capacity to maintain revenue exceeding costs over time
the financial attractiveness of a business, market, product, or customer relationship

nuance.ja: profitability は利益額そのものではなく、事業がどれだけ効果的・継続的に利益を生み出せるかという性質や程度を表す。大企業は利益の絶対額が大きくても、売上高や投下資本に対する利益率が低ければ profitability は低い場合がある。反対に、小規模な事業でも利益率が高ければ収益性は高いと評価できる。profit margin、return on assets、return on equity など、どの指標を使うかによって評価は変わる。短期的な費用削減は当期の profitability を改善しても、研究開発や人材への投資を損なえば長期的な収益性を低下させる可能性がある。
nuance.en: Profitability concerns the capacity or degree of generating profit rather than merely the absolute amount of profit earned. A large company may report a substantial profit but still have low profitability if that amount is small relative to its sales or invested capital. Conversely, a small business may be highly profitable when it earns a strong margin. The assessment varies according to the measure used, such as profit margin, return on assets, or return on equity. Cost reductions may improve current profitability while damaging long-term profitability if they undermine research, product quality, or investment in employees.

ja: profitability：売上げ・資産・資本などに対して利益を生み出す能力・程度、収益性。
profit：収益から費用を差し引いた後に残る利益額。
revenue：商品・サービスの販売などから得た総収入。費用は差し引かない。
profit margin：売上高のうち利益が占める割合、利益率。
return on investment：投資額に対して得られた利益・成果の割合。
cash flow：一定期間に企業へ入る現金と企業から出る現金の流れ。
solvency：長期的な債務を履行できる財務上の能力。
competitiveness：市場で競合と争い、成功を収める能力・競争力。
en: profitability is the ability or degree to which profit is generated relative to sales, assets, capital, or other resources.
profit is the amount remaining after expenses have been deducted from revenue.
revenue is total income from sales or other operations before expenses are deducted.
profit margin is the proportion of sales revenue remaining as profit.
return on investment measures the profit or benefit obtained relative to the amount invested.
cash flow is the movement of cash into and out of a business during a period.
solvency is the financial ability to meet long-term debts and obligations.
competitiveness is the ability to compete successfully against rivals in a market.

etymology.ja: profitability は profitable に性質・状態を表す接尾辞 -ity が付いて成立した。profitable は profit と -able から成る。profit は古フランス語 profit を経て、ラテン語 profectus「進歩、前進、利益」に由来し、proficere「前進する、役立つ」と関係する。もともと「前進・有益な結果」を意味したものが、商業上の金銭的利益を表すようになった。profitability は、そのような利益を生み出せる性質・能力を意味する。
etymology.en: Profitability was formed from profitable and the quality-forming suffix -ity. Profitable consists of profit and -able. Profit entered English through Old French profit from Latin profectus, progress, advance, or benefit, related to proficere, to advance or be useful. The general idea of beneficial progress developed into the commercial meaning of financial gain. Profitability consequently denotes the quality or capacity of producing such gain.

note.ja: 企業・資産・投資などが将来にわたって収益や利益を生み出す能力。
note.en: The ability of a company, asset, or investment to generate earnings or profit over time.

note.ja: 事業・製品・投資が将来的に利益を生み出す可能性。
note.en: The possibility that a business, product, or investment will generate profit in the future.

note.ja: 利益・収益・費用・資産などから評価される、企業の財務上の成果全般。
note.en: The broader financial results of a business as assessed through profit, revenue, costs, assets, and related measures.

note.ja: 投資した金銭・資本に対して得られる利益・収益。
note.en: The profit or income received in relation to money or capital invested.

note.ja: 仕事・市場・取引などが多額の利益をもたらす性質。profitability より評価的。
note.en: The quality of producing substantial profit, with a more evaluative tone than profitability.

ja: The company increased its profitability by reducing unnecessary operating costs. — その会社は不要な運営費を削減することで収益性を高めた。

usage.shape: Crooked describes something bent, curved, twisted, or not positioned in a straight or level manner.
usage.body: It commonly modifies teeth, fingers, a nose, a back, or a smile when their shape is irregular or asymmetrical.
usage.dishonesty: Informally, it describes a dishonest or corrupt person, organization, transaction, or practice.
usage.pronunciation: As an adjective, crooked is pronounced with two syllables, /ˈkrʊkɪd/.
usage.comparison: More crooked and most crooked are common; crookeder and crookedest also occur, especially in informal descriptions of physical shape.
usage.evaluation: When applied to a person, crooked is strongly accusatory and may imply fraud, corruption, or criminal conduct.

ja: まっすぐでなく、曲がった・ねじれた
水平・垂直でなく、傾いた・ゆがんだ
歯・鼻・指などの形が不ぞろいな
道・川・線などが曲がりくねった
人・取引・組織などが不正・腐敗に関わる
笑顔などが左右非対称で、少しゆがんだ
en: bent, twisted, or not forming a straight line
not level, vertical, or correctly aligned
irregular in shape, especially of teeth, a nose, or fingers
winding and changing direction repeatedly, especially of a road, river, or line
dishonest, corrupt, or involved in illegal conduct
for a smile, asymmetrical or slightly twisted

nuance.ja: crooked の中心的な意味は、基準となるまっすぐな線・正しい位置から外れて曲がっていることである。a crooked picture は壁に斜めに掛かった絵、crooked teeth は歯並びの不ぞろいな歯を表す。そこから道徳的に「正道」から外れているという比喩が生まれ、a crooked politician は賄賂・詐欺などに関わる腐敗した政治家を意味する。bent も物理的な曲がりと不正の両方を表せるが、crooked の方が外形の不規則さや犯罪的な不正を直接的に感じさせる。人を crooked と断定するのは強い非難になる。
nuance.en: The central idea of crooked is deviation from a straight line or proper alignment. A crooked picture hangs at an angle, while crooked teeth are irregularly aligned. This physical departure from straightness produced a moral metaphor of departing from the proper path: a crooked politician is corrupt and may be involved in bribery, fraud, or other illegal conduct. Bent can also describe both physical curvature and dishonesty, but crooked more readily evokes an irregular shape or directly criminal corruption. Calling a person crooked is therefore a serious accusation rather than a mild criticism.

ja: crooked：形・位置が曲がった、ゆがんだ。または人・取引などが不正な。
bent：圧力・損傷などによって曲がった。人については不正な意味にもなる。
curved：滑らかな曲線を描いている。欠陥・不正という含みはない。
twisted：複数方向へねじれた。または考え・性格が倒錯した。
uneven：表面・高さ・間隔・品質などが均一でない。
askew：正しい位置から斜めに傾いている。副詞・形容詞。
dishonest：嘘・詐欺などによって誠実さを欠くことを直接的に表す。
corrupt：権力を私的利益のため不正に利用する、または制度が腐敗した。
en: crooked describes something bent or misaligned, or a person or transaction that is dishonest or corrupt.
bent describes something curved by pressure or damage and can also informally mean dishonest.
curved describes a smooth rounded shape without implying defect or dishonesty.
twisted describes something turned irregularly in multiple directions or figuratively a distorted mind or character.
uneven means not uniform in surface, height, spacing, quality, or distribution.
askew means positioned at an incorrect angle rather than straight or level.
dishonest directly describes conduct involving lies, fraud, or lack of integrity.
corrupt describes abuse of power for private gain or an institution seriously affected by such conduct.

etymology.ja: crooked は動詞 crook「曲げる」に過去分詞・形容詞語尾 -ed が付いた形である。crook は古ノルド語 krókr「鉤、曲がった物」に由来し、先端の曲がった杖や鉤を表した。物理的に曲がっているという意味から、正しい道・道徳的な直線から外れるという比喩が生まれ、「不正な、腐敗した」という意味へ発展した。名詞 crook が「詐欺師、犯罪者」を表す用法も同じ比喩に基づく。
etymology.en: Crooked was formed from the verb crook, to bend, and the participial adjective ending -ed. Crook derives from Old Norse krókr, a hook or bent object, and originally referred to a hooked implement or curved staff. Physical deviation from straightness became a metaphor for departing from an honest or morally correct path. This produced the meaning dishonest or corrupt, as well as the related noun crook for a criminal or fraudster.

note.ja: 力・圧力・使用などにより、元のまっすぐな形から曲がっている。
note.en: Forced or changed from an originally straight shape through pressure, damage, or use.

note.ja: 物が正しい位置・角度からずれ、斜めに傾いている。
note.en: Positioned at an incorrect angle or displaced from its proper alignment.

note.ja: 嘘・欺罔・不正な行為などにより、誠実さや信用性を欠く。
note.en: Lacking integrity or trustworthiness through lying, deception, or improper conduct.

note.ja: 地位・権力を利用し、賄賂その他の私的利益を不正に得ようとする。
note.en: Willing to abuse a position or authority to obtain bribes or other private advantages.

note.ja: 目的を達成するため、率直でない策略的・欺瞞的な方法を用いる。
note.en: Using indirect, secretive, or deceptive methods to achieve an objective.

usage.correction: In fact can correct a previous statement or assumption by introducing more accurate information.
usage.emphasis: It can emphasize that a statement is true, especially when the fact may be surprising or disputed.
usage.addition: It may strengthen a preceding statement by adding a more striking or specific fact.
usage.contrast: It often introduces information contrary to what was expected: I thought it was difficult; in fact, it was easy.
usage.punctuation: At the beginning of a sentence, it is normally followed by a comma. In medial position, commas are common when it is parenthetical.
usage.register: It is natural in both conversation and formal writing, although excessive use can make prose sound argumentative.

ja: 実際には、事実としては
予想・印象・先の発言とは異なる事実を示して
より正確に言えば、実のところ
直前の主張をさらに強める事実を付け加えて
疑われる可能性のある内容が本当であることを強調して
en: in reality or as a matter of actual fact
used to introduce information contrary to an expectation, impression, or previous statement
used to provide a more accurate account of a situation
used to strengthen a preceding statement with a more striking fact
used to emphasize that a possibly surprising or disputed statement is true

nuance.ja: in fact は、現実の事実と予想・外見・先の発言とのずれを示したり、直前の主張をさらに強めたりする談話標識である。I thought he was French. In fact, he’s Belgian. では誤った認識を訂正し、The task was difficult. In fact, it took three days. では具体的事実を加えて困難さを強調する。actually と近いが、actually は会話で相手を訂正したり、意外な事実を述べたりする際により広く使われる。indeed は先の主張への同意・強調に向き、必ずしも訂正を伴わない。as a matter of fact は意味が近いが、やや長く、会話では反論・訂正の響きが強くなる場合がある。
nuance.en: In fact is a discourse marker used to contrast reality with an expectation, appearance, or earlier statement, or to reinforce a claim with stronger information. I thought he was French. In fact, he’s Belgian corrects a mistaken belief, whereas The task was difficult. In fact, it took three days adds evidence strengthening the first statement. Actually overlaps with in fact but is especially common in conversation and has a wider range of corrective and surprising uses. Indeed is particularly suited to confirmation and emphasis and need not introduce a correction. As a matter of fact has a similar meaning but is longer and can sound more explicitly corrective or argumentative.

ja: in fact：予想・印象を訂正し、または直前の主張を強めて「実際には、事実」。
actually：実際には、本当は。特に会話で訂正・意外な情報を導入する。
as a matter of fact：実を言うと、事実として。in fact より長く、反論的に響くことがある。
indeed：確かに、実に。先の発言への同意や強い確認・強調に使う。
in reality：見かけ・想像とは異なる現実を強調する。
in truth：真実を言えば、実際には。やや形式的・文語的。
to be precise：数値・表現・内容を、より正確な形に言い直す。
on the contrary：先の否定的な内容とは正反対であることを明示する。
en: in fact corrects an expectation or strengthens a previous statement by introducing the actual facts.
actually introduces a correction or surprising reality and is especially common in conversation.
as a matter of fact has a similar meaning but is longer and may sound more argumentative.
indeed confirms, agrees with, or strongly emphasizes a preceding statement.
in reality emphasizes the true situation as opposed to appearance or imagination.
in truth means according to the truth and has a somewhat formal or literary tone.
to be precise introduces a more exact reformulation of a number, expression, or statement.
on the contrary explicitly introduces a proposition opposite to something just denied.

etymology.ja: fact はラテン語 factum「なされたこと、行為、出来事」に由来し、これは facere「行う、作る」の過去分詞 factus と関係する。「実際になされたこと」から、証明可能な現実・真実という意味が発達した。in fact は本来「現実に起きた事柄において」という構造を持ち、外見・推測・理論ではなく実際の事実を示す副詞句として定着した。
etymology.en: Fact comes from Latin factum, a deed, event, or thing done, related to factus, the past participle of facere, to do or make. From the idea of something actually done, fact developed the meaning of a verifiable reality or truth. In fact originally had the structural sense in what was actually done or existing and became established as an adverbial phrase contrasting reality with appearance, assumption, or theory.

note.ja: 予想や先の発言を訂正したり、意外な現実を示したりする、特に会話で一般的な語。
note.en: A common word, especially in conversation, for correcting an expectation or introducing a surprising reality.

note.ja: 実際の事情を述べて訂正・反論・強調する表現で、in fact より長い。
note.en: A longer expression introducing actual circumstances for correction, contradiction, or emphasis.

note.ja: 発言の真実性・程度を強調し、または相手の発言に強く同意する。
note.en: Emphasizes the truth or degree of a statement or expresses strong agreement with another speaker.

note.ja: 外見・期待・想像と対比して、実際の状態や現実を示す。
note.en: Introduces the actual situation in contrast with appearance, expectation, or imagination.

note.ja: 外見や一般的な認識とは異なる真実を述べる、やや形式的な表現。
note.en: A somewhat formal expression introducing the truth behind appearances or general assumptions.

usage.emphasis: Indeed emphasizes that a statement or degree is certainly true: very difficult indeed.
usage.confirmation: It can confirm or strongly agree with a preceding statement: It was an excellent result indeed.
usage.response: Indeed. can express formal agreement, while Indeed? may express surprise, doubt, or a request for confirmation.
usage.addition: It can introduce a stronger or more specific statement supporting what came before.
usage.concession: In the pattern indeed ... but, it acknowledges one point before introducing a qualification or contrast.
usage.register: Indeed is common in formal writing and British English conversation; as a standalone response it may sound formal, restrained, ironic, or old-fashioned depending on tone.

ja: 発言の真実性・確実性を強める「確かに、実に」
形容詞・副詞の程度を強調する「本当に、まったく」
先の主張を確認し、強く同意する「そのとおり」
先の内容をさらに強める事実・説明を付け加える「それどころか」
ある点を認めたうえで、反対・留保を続ける「確かに～だが」
疑問調で、驚き・疑い・確認を表す「本当ですか」
en: used to emphasize the truth or certainty of a statement
used to intensify the degree expressed by an adjective or adverb
used to confirm or express strong agreement with a preceding statement
used to add a stronger fact or explanation supporting what was just said
used to concede one point before introducing a contrast or qualification
with questioning intonation, used to express surprise, doubt, or a request for confirmation

nuance.ja: indeed は、事実を訂正するというより、発言が確かに正しいことを確認・強調する語である。The task was difficult indeed. は「その仕事は実に難しかった」と程度を強める。Indeed, it was impossible. なら、先の「難しかった」という評価をさらに強めて「実際、不可能だった」と続ける。in fact は予想や先の発言との食い違いを訂正する働きが強いのに対し、indeed は先の内容を支持・確認することが多い。単独の Indeed. は「まったくそのとおりです」だが、日常会話では話し方によって、格式ばった、冷淡な、または皮肉な響きになることがある。
nuance.en: Indeed primarily confirms or strengthens a statement rather than correcting it. The task was difficult indeed intensifies the degree of difficulty. Indeed, it was impossible may follow an observation that the task was difficult and replace it with an even stronger supporting statement. In fact more readily corrects an assumption or contrasts reality with a previous claim, whereas indeed usually endorses or reinforces what came before. As a standalone response, Indeed. means certainly or quite so, but in casual conversation it can sound formal, restrained, old-fashioned, or ironic depending on intonation.

ja: indeed：発言を確認・強調して「確かに、実に」。先の内容をさらに強めることもある。
in fact：予想・印象を訂正し、または実際の事実によって先の主張を強める。
actually：会話で予想・誤解を訂正し、意外な現実を述べる。
certainly：発言の確実性・同意・承諾を明確に表す。
truly：内容が偽りでないこと、または程度が非常に高いことを感情的に強調する。
really：真実性または程度を強める、日常会話で最も一般的な語。
in reality：外見・想像・理論と対比して、現実の状態を示す。
admittedly：不利または譲歩すべき点を認めてから、反論・限定を続ける。
en: indeed confirms or emphasizes a statement and may introduce an even stronger supporting point.
in fact corrects an expectation or strengthens a claim by introducing the actual facts.
actually commonly introduces a correction or surprising reality in conversation.
certainly clearly expresses confidence, agreement, or willingness.
truly emotionally emphasizes genuineness or an exceptionally high degree.
really is the most common conversational intensifier of truth or degree.
in reality contrasts the actual situation with appearance, imagination, or theory.
admittedly concedes a potentially unfavorable point before a qualification or counterargument.

etymology.ja: indeed は中英語の in dede「行為において、実際に」に由来する。deed は古英語 dǣd「行為、なされたこと」にさかのぼり、do と同じ語族に属する。「言葉の上だけでなく実際の行為において」という意味から、「現実に、確かに」という副詞になり、さらに同意・確認・程度の強調を表す談話標識へ発達した。
etymology.en: Indeed developed from Middle English in dede, literally in deed or in actual action. Deed comes from Old English dǣd, an act or thing done, and belongs to the same word family as do. The phrase originally contrasted actual conduct with mere words. It consequently developed the meanings in reality and certainly and later became a discourse marker expressing confirmation, agreement, and emphasis.

note.ja: 発言が確実に正しいこと、相手への同意、または依頼への快い承諾を明確に表す。
note.en: Clearly expresses that something is unquestionably true, agreement with another person, or willingness to comply.

note.ja: 内容が本当であること、または性質・程度が非常に強いことを感情を込めて強調する。
note.en: Emphasizes with some emotional force that something is genuine or possesses a quality to a high degree.

note.ja: 現実の事実を示して予想・認識を訂正し、または直前の主張を強める。
note.en: Introduces actual facts to correct an expectation or reinforce a preceding statement.

note.ja: 疑いの余地がないほど確実であるという話者の強い判断を表す。
note.en: Expresses the speaker’s strong judgment that something is true beyond reasonable doubt.

note.ja: 確実に、間違いなくという強い確認を表す、形式的でやや古風な語。
note.en: A formal and somewhat old-fashioned adverb expressing strong certainty or confirmation.

ja: very good indeed — 実に良い
very difficult indeed — 本当に難しい
very fortunate indeed — 実に幸運な
a serious problem indeed — 確かに深刻な問題
Yes, indeed — まったくそのとおり
Indeed, this is true — 確かに、これは事実である
and indeed — そして実際、それどころか
if indeed this is the case — 仮に本当にそうであるなら
whether indeed it is possible — それが本当に可能かどうか
was indeed correct — 確かに正しかった
did indeed happen — 確かに起こった
may indeed be necessary — 実際に必要かもしれない
en: very good indeed
very difficult indeed
very fortunate indeed
a serious problem indeed
Yes, indeed
Indeed, this is true
and indeed
if indeed this is the case
whether indeed it is possible
was indeed correct
did indeed happen
may indeed be necessary

ja: The view from the top of the mountain was beautiful indeed. — 山頂からの眺めは実に美しかった。
“Was the meeting difficult?” “Yes, indeed.” — 「会議は難航しましたか」「ええ、まったくそのとおりです」
The problem is serious; indeed, it may be more serious than we first believed. — 問題は深刻であり、実際、当初考えていたより深刻かもしれない。
The proposal is ambitious indeed, but its cost remains a major concern. — その提案が確かに意欲的であることは認めるが、費用は依然として大きな懸念である。
The cited document is indeed relevant, but it does not disclose every limitation of the patent claim. — 引用文献に確かに関連性はあるが、特許請求項のすべての構成要件を開示しているわけではない。
en: The view from the top of the mountain was beautiful indeed.
“Was the meeting difficult?” “Yes, indeed.”
The problem is serious; indeed, it may be more serious than we first believed.
The proposal is ambitious indeed, but its cost remains a major concern.
The cited document is indeed relevant, but it does not disclose every limitation of the patent claim.

grammar.countability: normally singular with the as a noun phrase
grammar.plural: not normally used in the advanced-frontier sense
patterns: be at the cutting edge of + field / technology
put someone at the cutting edge of + field
the cutting edge of + research / innovation
keep something at the cutting edge

usage.hyphenation: Use a hyphen when the expression modifies a noun: cutting-edge technology.
usage.noun: As a noun phrase meaning the most advanced position, it is normally written without a hyphen: the cutting edge of research.
usage.article: The figurative noun phrase normally takes the definite article: at the cutting edge, not at a cutting edge.
usage.literal: The literal cutting edge is the sharpened part of a knife, blade, or tool that performs the cutting.
usage.evaluation: The figurative adjective is strongly positive and often used in promotional language, so evidence may be needed when precision matters.
usage.temporality: What qualifies as cutting-edge changes as research, technology, and market practices develop.

ja: 技術・研究・設計などが、その時点で最も進んだ最先端の
新しい知識・方法を積極的に採用した革新的な
分野の発展を先導するほど高度な
the cutting edge の形で、研究・技術・活動の最前線
文字どおり、刃物・工具の物を切る鋭い部分、刃先
en: using or representing the most advanced technology, research, or design currently available
highly innovative through the adoption of new knowledge or methods
advanced enough to lead development in a particular field
in the cutting edge, the most advanced frontier of research, technology, or activity
literally, the sharpened part of a blade or tool that performs the cutting

nuance.ja: cutting-edge は、単に modern「現代的な」だけでなく、ある分野で現在到達している最も進んだ水準に位置することを表す。cutting-edge research は既存知識の最前線を押し広げる研究、a cutting-edge product は最新技術を採用した革新的な製品を意味する。一方、広告では客観的根拠が乏しくても製品を魅力的に見せるため使われることがある。state-of-the-art と近いが、cutting-edge は新規性・革新性・発展の最前線を、state-of-the-art は現時点で利用可能な最高水準を強調しやすい。特許性を意味する法律用語ではなく、cutting-edge であっても必ず新規・非自明とは限らない。
nuance.en: Cutting-edge means more than merely modern: it places something at the most advanced current frontier of a field. Cutting-edge research pushes the boundary of existing knowledge, while a cutting-edge product incorporates highly advanced or innovative technology. The expression is also common in advertising and may be used without rigorous objective support. It overlaps with state-of-the-art, but cutting-edge tends to emphasize innovation and movement at the frontier, whereas state-of-the-art emphasizes the highest level currently achieved or available. It is not a legal test of patentability, and cutting-edge technology is not necessarily novel or nonobvious in the patent-law sense.

ja: cutting-edge：研究・技術・設計などが現在の発展の最前線にある、最先端の。
state-of-the-art：現時点で達成・利用可能な最高水準の。
leading-edge：技術・研究・事業などの発展を先導する非常に先進的な。
advanced：通常より高度・発達しているが、必ずしも最先端とは限らない。
innovative：新しい発想・方法を導入し、従来とは異なる。
groundbreaking：重要な新領域・方法を切り開くほど画期的な。
pioneering：新しい分野・方法を他者に先駆けて開拓する。
modern：現在の時代に属し、旧式ではない。最先端という意味までは含まない。
en: cutting-edge describes research, technology, or design at the most advanced frontier of current development.
state-of-the-art describes the highest level currently achieved or available.
leading-edge describes highly advanced work or technology that helps lead development in a field.
advanced means highly developed or sophisticated but not necessarily at the absolute frontier.
innovative means introducing new ideas or methods that differ from established practice.
groundbreaking describes work opening an important new field or method.
pioneering describes being among the first to develop or use a new field, technique, or approach.
modern means belonging to the present era and not old-fashioned, without necessarily being cutting-edge.

etymology.ja: cutting edge は本来、ナイフ・剣・工具などで実際に対象へ接触して切断する最前部の刃先を意味する。cut は古英語には確認されない後期古英語・中英語期の語で、より古い起源は不確かである。edge は古英語 ecg「刃、鋭い縁」に由来する。刃先が物を切り開きながら最前方へ進むイメージから、技術・研究・思想などの発展の最前線を表す比喩的意味が生まれた。
etymology.en: The cutting edge literally denotes the forward sharpened part of a knife, sword, or tool that contacts and cuts material. The deeper origin of cut is uncertain, while edge derives from Old English ecg, a blade or sharp border. Because a cutting edge moves at the front and opens a path through material, it became a metaphor for the most advanced frontier of technology, research, thought, and other developing fields.

note.ja: 特定時点において達成されている、または利用可能な最高の技術水準を表す。
note.en: Describes the highest level of technological development achieved or available at a particular time.

note.ja: 発展の先頭に位置し、技術・研究・市場を先導するほど先進的な。
note.en: Positioned at the front of development and sufficiently advanced to lead technology, research, or a market.

note.ja: 従来と異なる新しい発想・技術・方法を導入している。
note.en: Introducing ideas, technology, or methods that are new and different from established practice.

note.ja: 既存の限界を破り、新しい分野・方法・理解を切り開くほど画期的な。
note.en: Important and original enough to open a new field, method, or understanding.

note.ja: 他者に先駆けて新しい研究・技術・活動を開始し、道を開く。
note.en: Being among the first to initiate and develop a new area of research, technology, or activity.

equivalents.de: hochmoderne / führend / auf dem neuesten Stand

ja: cutting-edge technology — 最先端技術
cutting-edge research — 最先端研究
a cutting-edge product — 最先端の製品
a cutting-edge technique — 最先端の技法
cutting-edge equipment — 最先端設備
a cutting-edge facility — 最先端施設
cutting-edge design — 最先端のデザイン
cutting-edge innovation — 最先端の革新
at the cutting edge — 最先端にあって
at the cutting edge of research — 研究の最前線にあって
remain at the cutting edge — 最先端の地位を維持する
the cutting edge of a blade — 刃物の刃先
en: cutting-edge technology
cutting-edge research
a cutting-edge product
a cutting-edge technique
cutting-edge equipment
a cutting-edge facility
cutting-edge design
cutting-edge innovation
at the cutting edge
at the cutting edge of research
remain at the cutting edge
the cutting edge of a blade

ja: The laboratory is developing cutting-edge medical technology. — その研究所は最先端の医療技術を開発している。
This university has remained at the cutting edge of robotics research. — この大学はロボット研究の最前線にあり続けている。
The company invested heavily in cutting-edge manufacturing equipment. — その会社は最先端の製造設備へ多額の投資を行った。
The advertisement describes the device as cutting-edge, but its basic technology is already widely available. — 広告はその装置を最先端と表現しているが、基礎となる技術はすでに広く利用可能である。
A product may use cutting-edge technology without being patentable if the claimed features are already disclosed in the prior art. — 製品が最先端技術を使用していても、請求された特徴がすでに先行技術に開示されていれば、特許性を有しないことがある。
en: The laboratory is developing cutting-edge medical technology.
This university has remained at the cutting edge of robotics research.
The company invested heavily in cutting-edge manufacturing equipment.
The advertisement describes the device as cutting-edge, but its basic technology is already widely available.
A product may use cutting-edge technology without being patentable if the claimed features are already disclosed in the prior art.

grammar.countability: normally uncountable; countable when referring to a particular act or instance
patterns: the obliteration of + place / object / evidence
the obliteration of a mark / inscription

usage.destruction: Obliteration may mean the complete or almost complete destruction of a place, object, group, or system.
usage.erasure: It can mean removing, covering, or damaging writing, marks, records, or evidence until they can no longer be read or recognized.
usage.figurative: It may describe the disappearance of a memory, identity, distinction, culture, or other abstract quality.
usage.medical: In medicine, it can refer to the closing, filling, or disappearance of a cavity, passage, space, or vessel.
usage.intensity: The word is much stronger than damage and normally suggests that recognition, existence, or function has almost entirely disappeared.
usage.register: It is formal and often dramatic; destruction, erasure, removal, or blockage may be clearer in ordinary contexts.

ja: 物・場所・組織などを完全またはほぼ完全に破壊すること
文字・印・記録などを読めない、または識別できない状態にすること
証拠・痕跡などを消し去ること
記憶・文化・個性・区別などが完全に失われること
医学的に、空洞・管・血管などが閉鎖・消失すること
en: the complete or nearly complete destruction of an object, place, organization, or system
the act of making writing, a mark, or a record unreadable or unrecognizable
the removal or destruction of evidence, traces, or other signs of existence
the complete loss of a memory, culture, identity, distinction, or other abstract quality
in medicine, the closing, filling, or disappearance of a cavity, passage, or vessel

nuance.ja: obliteration は、対象が単に損傷するのではなく、存在・形状・機能・識別可能性がほとんど失われるほど徹底的に破壊・消去されることを表す。the obliteration of a city は都市の壊滅、the obliteration of a signature は署名が読めなくなるほど消されることを意味する。比喩的には、文化・記憶・個性・二つの概念の区別が完全に消えることにも使える。annihilation と近いが、annihilation は存在そのものの消滅を、obliteration は破壊・上書き・摩耗などによって痕跡や識別可能性まで失わせることを強調しやすい。
nuance.en: Obliteration implies far more than ordinary damage. It suggests that an object’s existence, form, function, or recognizability has been almost entirely destroyed. The obliteration of a city describes devastating physical destruction, while the obliteration of a signature means that the signature has been erased, covered, or damaged until it is unreadable. Figuratively, the word can describe the disappearance of a culture, memory, identity, or conceptual distinction. Annihilation more directly emphasizes total nonexistence, whereas obliteration often emphasizes destroying or covering something so thoroughly that no recognizable trace remains.

ja: obliteration：対象の存在・機能・識別可能性や痕跡まで、ほぼ完全に破壊・消去すること。
destruction：物・制度などを壊し、存在または機能を損なうことを広く表す。
annihilation：対象を完全に消滅させ、何も残さないことを強く表す。
erasure：文字・記録・データ・記憶などを消すこと。
elimination：不要・危険な物や問題を取り除き、存在しない状態にすること。
devastation：場所・生活・感情などに広範かつ深刻な破壊・打撃を与えること。
effacement：表面の印・特徴・記憶・個性などを消して目立たなくすること。形式的。
deletion：文書・データなどから特定の文字・情報・項目を削除すること。
en: obliteration is destruction or erasure so complete that existence, function, recognizability, or visible traces are nearly lost.
destruction broadly means damaging something so that its existence or function is seriously impaired.
annihilation strongly emphasizes the total elimination of something’s existence.
erasure is the removal of writing, records, data, or memories.
elimination means removing an unwanted or dangerous thing or problem completely.
devastation is widespread and severe physical, social, or emotional destruction.
effacement formally means erasing or making surface features, memories, or individuality less visible.
deletion is the removal of particular words, information, or items from a document or data system.

etymology.ja: obliteration は動詞 obliterate に名詞接尾辞 -ion が付いた語である。obliterate はラテン語 oblitterare「文字を消す、抹消する」に由来し、ob-「～に向かって、上に」と littera「文字」から成る。原義は、文字の上に別の印を付けたり表面をこすったりして読めなくすることだった。そこから、痕跡を消すこと、さらに物や場所を徹底的に破壊して識別不能にすることへ意味が拡大した。
etymology.en: Obliteration was formed from obliterate and the noun-forming suffix -ion. Obliterate comes from Latin oblitterare, to erase or strike out letters, formed from ob-, against or over, and littera, letter. Its original sense involved marking over or rubbing writing until it became unreadable. The meaning broadened from erasing written marks to removing all traces and ultimately to destroying an object or place so thoroughly that it is no longer recognizable.

note.ja: 人・物・勢力などを完全に破壊し、存在しない状態にすることを極めて強く表す。
note.en: An exceptionally strong word for completely destroying a person, object, or force so that it ceases to exist.

note.ja: 物・場所・制度などを壊し、その構造・機能・存在を失わせることを広く表す。
note.en: A broad term for damaging an object, place, or system so that its structure, function, or existence is lost.

note.ja: 文字・画像・記録・データ・記憶などを消去する行為または結果。
note.en: The act or result of removing writing, images, records, data, or memories.

note.ja: 表面上の印・特徴、または人の個性・歴史などを消して認識しにくくすること。
note.en: The formal act of erasing or obscuring surface marks, distinctive features, identity, or history.

note.ja: 地域・社会・生活などに広範囲で極めて深刻な破壊や苦痛をもたらすこと。
note.en: Widespread and extremely serious destruction or suffering affecting a place, society, or way of life.

ja: complete obliteration — 完全な破壊・消滅
total obliteration — 徹底的な壊滅
near obliteration — ほぼ完全な消滅
the obliteration of a city — 都市の壊滅
the obliteration of evidence — 証拠の完全な抹消
the obliteration of a mark — 標章・印の抹消
the obliteration of an inscription — 碑文・刻印の消失
the obliteration of a distinction — 区別の完全な消失
the obliteration of memory — 記憶の消失
threaten something with obliteration — 何かを壊滅の危機にさらす
save something from obliteration — 何かを消滅から救う
result in obliteration — 完全な破壊・消失をもたらす
en: complete obliteration
total obliteration
near obliteration
the obliteration of a city
the obliteration of evidence
the obliteration of a mark
the obliteration of an inscription
the obliteration of a distinction
the obliteration of memory
threaten something with obliteration
save something from obliteration
result in obliteration

ja: The explosion caused the near obliteration of the building. — その爆発によって建物はほぼ完全に破壊された。
Centuries of exposure to wind and rain resulted in the obliteration of the inscription. — 数世紀にわたって風雨にさらされた結果、碑文は完全に読めなくなった。
The historian warned against the obliteration of minority cultures. — その歴史家は、少数派文化が消滅する危険について警告した。
The alteration caused the obliteration of several important entries in the document. — その改変によって、文書中の複数の重要な記載が判読不能になった。

The obliteration of the original trademark from the packaging may affect whether consumers continue to perceive the goods as originating from the trademark owner. — 包装から元の商標を完全に抹消することは、需要者が商品を引き続き商標権者に由来するものと認識するかどうかに影響し得る。
en: The explosion caused the near obliteration of the building.
Centuries of exposure to wind and rain resulted in the obliteration of the inscription.
The historian warned against the obliteration of minority cultures.
The alteration caused the obliteration of several important entries in the document.
The obliteration of the original trademark from the packaging may affect whether consumers continue to perceive the goods as originating from the trademark owner.

patterns: obliterate all / every trace of + noun

usage.destruction: Obliterate means destroying something so completely that it no longer exists or can no longer be recognized.
usage.erasure: It can mean removing, covering, or damaging writing, marks, or evidence until they become unreadable or unidentifiable.
usage.memory: Obliterate something from memory means causing it to be forgotten completely.
usage.figurative: It can describe the destruction of a distinction, identity, culture, reputation, or other abstract quality.
usage.competition: Informally, it may mean defeating an opponent by an overwhelming margin.
usage.intensity: It is substantially stronger than damage, weaken, or defeat and can sound exaggerated when complete destruction is not intended.

ja: 物・場所などを跡形もないほど完全に破壊する
文字・印・記録などを読めない、または識別できない状態にする
証拠・痕跡・記憶などを完全に消し去る
文化・個性・区別などを失わせ、認識できなくする
口語的に、試合・競争で相手を圧倒的に打ち負かす
en: to destroy an object or place so completely that little or nothing recognizable remains
to erase, cover, or damage writing, marks, or records until they cannot be read or identified
to remove every trace of evidence, memory, or previous existence
to eliminate a culture, identity, individuality, or distinction
informally, to defeat an opponent by an overwhelming margin

nuance.ja: obliterate は、単に damage「損傷させる」のではなく、対象の存在・形・機能・識別可能性がほとんど失われるまで破壊・消去することを表す強い動詞である。The village was obliterated by the explosion. なら、村が認識できないほど壊滅したことを示す。文字や印については、削る・塗りつぶす・上書きするなどして判読不能にする意味になる。比喩的には、記憶や概念上の区別を完全に消すことにも使える。スポーツの We obliterated them. は「大差で圧勝した」という誇張的でくだけた用法であり、物理的な破壊を意味しない。
nuance.en: Obliterate is a powerful verb meaning much more than damage. It suggests destroying or erasing something until its existence, form, function, or recognizability is almost completely lost. The village was obliterated by the explosion indicates devastation so extensive that little identifiable structure remained. Applied to words or marks, it can mean scraping, covering, or writing over them until they are unreadable. Figuratively, it may describe completely eliminating a memory or conceptual distinction. In sports, We obliterated them is an informal exaggeration meaning that one side won by a very large margin, not that anyone was physically destroyed.

ja: obliterate：存在・形・機能・痕跡が分からなくなるほど、完全に破壊・消去する。
destroy：物・制度・関係などを壊し、存在・機能を失わせる一般的な語。
annihilate：対象を完全に消滅させる。obliterate と同様に非常に強い。
erase：文字・データ・記憶・印などを消す。
delete：文書・データから特定の情報・項目を削除する。
efface：表面の印・特徴・記憶などを消し去る。形式的。
devastate：場所・社会・人の感情などに壊滅的な被害・打撃を与える。
eliminate：不要・危険な対象を取り除き、存在しない状態にする。
en: obliterate means destroying or erasing something so completely that its form, function, or traces become unrecognizable.
destroy is the general verb for damaging something until its existence or function is lost.
annihilate is an exceptionally strong verb meaning to eliminate something completely.
erase means removing writing, data, memories, or marks.
delete means removing particular information or an item from a document or data system.
efface formally means erasing a surface mark, distinctive feature, or memory.
devastate means causing overwhelming physical, social, economic, or emotional damage.
eliminate means removing an unwanted or dangerous thing so that it no longer remains.

etymology.ja: obliterate はラテン語 oblitterare「文字を消す、抹消する」に由来し、ob-「～に向かって、上に」と littera「文字」から成る。原義は、文字の上を塗る、こする、別の印を付けるなどして読めなくすることだった。そこから、文字以外の痕跡を消す意味へ広がり、さらに物・場所などを識別不能になるほど徹底的に破壊することを表すようになった。名詞形は obliteration である。
etymology.en: Obliterate comes from Latin oblitterare, to erase or strike out letters, formed from ob-, against or over, and littera, letter. It originally meant rubbing, covering, or marking over writing until it could no longer be read. The sense expanded to removing other kinds of traces and then to destroying an object or place so completely that it becomes unrecognizable. Its corresponding noun is obliteration.

note.ja: 人・物・勢力などを完全に破壊し、存在しない状態にすることを極めて強く表す。
note.en: An exceptionally strong verb for completely destroying a person, object, or force so that it ceases to exist.

note.ja: 物・場所・制度などに重大な損傷を与え、その存在または機能を失わせる。
note.en: To damage an object, place, or system so severely that its existence or function is lost.

note.ja: 文字・印・データ・記憶などを表面・媒体・意識から消す。
note.en: To remove writing, marks, data, or memories from a surface, medium, or consciousness.

note.ja: 外観上の特徴・記録・記憶・個性などを消して認識しにくくする、形式的な語。
note.en: A formal verb meaning to erase or obscure visible features, records, memories, or individuality.

note.ja: 集団・物・記録・資産などを完全に破壊・消滅させる口語的な表現。
note.en: An informal phrasal verb meaning to destroy or eliminate a group, object, record, or asset completely.

ja: completely obliterate something — 何かを完全に破壊・消去する
virtually obliterate something — 何かを事実上消滅させる
obliterate a city — 都市を壊滅させる
obliterate a building — 建物を跡形もなく破壊する
obliterate evidence — 証拠を完全に消す
obliterate a record — 記録を抹消する
obliterate a word — 単語を判読不能にする
obliterate an inscription — 碑文・刻印を消す
obliterate a trademark — 商標を識別不能にする
obliterate a distinction — 区別を完全に失わせる
obliterate something from memory — 何かを記憶から完全に消す
obliterate the opposition — 反対勢力・対戦相手を圧倒する
en: completely obliterate something
virtually obliterate something
obliterate a city
obliterate a building
obliterate evidence
obliterate a record
obliterate a word
obliterate an inscription
obliterate a trademark
obliterate a distinction

ja: The explosion obliterated several buildings near the port. — その爆発は、港の近くにある複数の建物を跡形もなく破壊した。
Water damage had almost obliterated the writing on the document. — 水濡れによって、文書の文字はほとんど判読不能になっていた。
She wished she could obliterate the embarrassing incident from her memory. — 彼女は、その恥ずかしい出来事を記憶から完全に消せればよいのにと思った。
Standardized development must not obliterate the neighborhood’s cultural identity. — 画一的な開発によって、その地区の文化的個性が消されてはならない。

Removing the label may not be sufficient if the original trademark remains visible; it must be completely obliterated if the transaction requires its removal. — ラベルを剥がすだけでは、元の商標が見える状態で残るなら十分でないことがあり、取引上その除去が必要であれば完全に識別不能にしなければならない。
en: The explosion obliterated several buildings near the port.
Water damage had almost obliterated the writing on the document.
She wished she could obliterate the embarrassing incident from her memory.
Standardized development must not obliterate the neighborhood’s cultural identity.
Removing the label may not be sufficient if the original trademark remains visible; it must be completely obliterated if the transaction requires its removal.

grammar.countability: countable as a noun
patterns: design / develop / build a humanoid robot

usage.adjective: As an adjective, humanoid describes something having a form, structure, or appearance resembling that of a human.
usage.noun: As a countable noun, a humanoid is a robot, creature, or fictional being with a generally human-like form.
usage.robotics: A humanoid robot is designed with a body arrangement approximating the human form, although the degree of resemblance varies.
usage.function: Humanoid does not necessarily mean that the robot thinks, behaves, speaks, or possesses intelligence like a human.
usage.android: Android often suggests a robot or artificial being with a more convincingly human appearance, but the distinction is not applied consistently.
usage.anthropomorphic: Anthropomorphic is broader and can describe nonhuman things given human appearance, behavior, emotions, or personality.

ja: 形・身体構造・外見などが人間に似た
頭・胴体・腕・脚など、人間型の身体配置を持つ
名詞として、人間に似た形のロボット・生物・架空の存在
humanoid robot の形で、人型ロボット
必ずしも人間そっくりではないが、全体的な形態が人間型の
en: having a form, bodily structure, or appearance resembling that of a human
having a human-like arrangement of a head, torso, arms, and legs
as a noun, a robot, creature, or fictional being with a generally human form
in humanoid robot, a robot designed with a body approximating the human form
human-shaped overall without necessarily possessing a highly realistic human appearance

nuance.ja: humanoid の中心は知能ではなく形態である。humanoid robot は通常、人間に近い胴体・頭部・腕・脚などを備え、人間用に設計された環境や道具を利用できるよう構成されたロボットを指す。ただし、二足歩行、両腕、五本指、人間らしい顔のすべてを必ず備えるという一律の条件があるわけではない。android は特に外見まで人間と見分けにくい人工存在を示唆することが多いが、SFや一般用法では humanoid と重なる。anthropomorphic は形だけでなく、動物・物・ソフトウェアなどに人間の感情・人格・行動を与える場合にも使える、より広い語である。
nuance.en: Humanoid primarily concerns form rather than intelligence. A humanoid robot typically has a human-like arrangement of torso, head, arms, or legs and may be designed to operate in environments and use tools made for humans. There is no single universal requirement that every humanoid must walk on two legs, have two complete arms, possess five-fingered hands, or display a realistic face. Android often suggests an artificial being whose outward appearance is especially close to that of a human, although ordinary and science-fiction usage overlaps. Anthropomorphic is broader and can describe animals, objects, or software given human emotions, personality, behavior, or form.

ja: humanoid：全体的な形・身体構造が人間に似たもの、またはそのようなロボット・存在。
humanoid robot：人間型の身体構造を持つよう設計されたロボット。
android：特に外見・行動が人間に酷似した人工的存在を指すことが多い。
robot：自動的またはプログラムに従って作業する機械。人間型とは限らない。
anthropomorphic：非人間の物・動物などに、人間の姿・感情・性格を持たせた。
bipedal：二本の脚で立つ、または歩行する。人間型であるとは限らない。
cyborg：生物の身体と人工的・機械的な部品を組み合わせた存在。
automaton：自動的に動作する機械・人形、または機械的に行動する人。
en: humanoid describes something with an overall form or bodily structure resembling that of a human.
a humanoid robot is a robot designed with a body arrangement approximating the human form.
an android often means an artificial being whose appearance or behavior closely resembles a human.
a robot is a machine that performs tasks automatically or under programmed control and need not be human-shaped.
anthropomorphic describes a nonhuman thing or animal given human form, emotions, personality, or behavior.
bipedal means standing or walking on two legs and does not necessarily mean humanoid.
a cyborg combines a biological organism with artificial or mechanical components.
an automaton is a self-operating machine or figure, or figuratively a person behaving mechanically.

etymology.ja: humanoid は human と、形・類似性を表す接尾辞 -oid から成る。human はラテン語 humanus「人間の、人間らしい」に由来する。-oid はギリシャ語 eidos「形、姿」に由来し、android「人間に似たもの」、spheroid「球状のもの」などにも見られる。したがって humanoid は文字どおりには「人間のような形を持つもの」を意味し、当初は人間に似た生物・架空の存在などに使われ、後にロボット工学の用語として広く用いられるようになった。
etymology.en: Humanoid is formed from human and the suffix -oid, indicating form or resemblance. Human derives from Latin humanus, human or relating to humankind. The suffix -oid comes from Greek eidos, form or appearance, and also occurs in words such as android and spheroid. Humanoid therefore literally means having a human-like form. It was applied to human-shaped creatures and fictional beings and later became widely established in robotics.

note.ja: 外見・行動・声・能力など、何らかの点で人間に似ていることを広く表す。
note.en: A broad expression for resembling humans in appearance, behavior, voice, ability, or another respect.

note.ja: 動物・物・神・システムなどに、人間の姿・感情・意図・人格を与えた。
note.en: Describes an animal, object, deity, or system given human form, emotion, intention, or personality.

note.ja: 一般に、外見や行動が人間に非常によく似たロボット・人工生命体。
note.en: Generally, a robot or artificial being whose appearance or behavior closely resembles that of a human.

note.ja: 知能・動作などについて含意せず、外形が人間の形をしていることを直接表す。
note.en: Directly describes an object’s human form without implying intelligence or human-like behavior.

note.ja: 人間に似た形を持つという意味だが、現代では主に類人猿に関する生物学的文脈で使われる。
note.en: Means human-like in form but is now used mainly in biological contexts relating to apes.

a bipedal humanoid robot — 二足歩行型の人型ロボット

ja: The company demonstrated a humanoid robot capable of carrying boxes. — その会社は、箱を運ぶことのできる人型ロボットを実演した。
The machine has a humanoid body but no human-like face. — その機械は人間型の身体を持つが、人間らしい顔は備えていない。
Researchers are teaching the humanoid to maintain its balance on uneven ground. — 研究者たちは、その人型ロボットに不整地でバランスを保つ方法を学習させている。
A robot can be intelligent and autonomous without being humanoid. — ロボットは人間型でなくても、高度な知能と自律性を持つことができる。
The patent claim covers a control system for humanoid robots but does not require the robot to have a realistic human appearance. — その特許請求項は人型ロボットの制御システムを対象としているが、ロボットが写実的な人間の外見を持つことまでは要求していない。

The machine has a humanoid body but no human-like face.
Researchers are teaching the humanoid to maintain its balance on uneven ground.
A robot can be intelligent and autonomous without being humanoid.

grammar.countability: normally uncountable as a noun
grammar.transitivity: transitive; occasionally intransitive in specialized use
patterns: a room / desk full of clutter

usage.uncountable: Clutter is normally uncountable: too much clutter, not many clutters.
usage.noun: As a noun, it means an untidy or excessive collection of objects or information that makes a space difficult to use or understand.
usage.verb: As a verb, it means filling a place, screen, document, or communication with too many unnecessary things.
usage.preposition: With introduces the objects or details causing congestion: The desk was cluttered with papers.
usage.phrasal_verb: Clutter up has the same basic meaning but is more conversational and emphasizes obstructing or overcrowding a space.
usage.evaluation: Clutter normally has a negative meaning, although a cluttered space may occasionally be described affectionately as lively or comfortably untidy.

ja: 部屋・机などに乱雑に置かれた多数の物、散らかった物
空間の利用や移動を妨げる不要な物の集まり
画面・文書・説明などを見づらくする過剰な情報・要素
動詞として、場所を多数の物で散らかす・ふさぐ
不要な細部・画像・情報などを加えて内容を分かりにくくする
en: an untidy collection of numerous objects in a room, on a desk, or in another place
unnecessary items occupying space and interfering with movement or use
excessive information or visual elements making a screen, document, or explanation difficult to understand
as a verb, to fill or obstruct a place with too many objects
to make content less clear by adding unnecessary details, images, or information

nuance.ja: clutter は、単に物が整然としていないだけでなく、物や情報が多すぎて、空間の利用・移動・理解を妨げている状態を表す。a cluttered desk は書類や道具が多く散らかった机、a cluttered interface はボタン・文字・画像が多すぎて使いにくい画面である。mess は汚れ・混乱・失敗を含むさらに広い語だが、clutter は主として「多すぎる物が場所を占めること」に焦点を置く。動詞では clutter a page with technical details のように、不要な要素を加えて本筋を見えにくくする比喩的用法も一般的である。
nuance.en: Clutter implies not merely a lack of neat arrangement but an excessive quantity of objects or information interfering with the use, movement, or comprehension of a space. A cluttered desk contains too many papers or tools, while a cluttered interface has so many buttons, words, or images that it becomes difficult to use. Mess is broader and may include dirt, confusion, or failure, whereas clutter focuses particularly on too many things occupying space. The verb is also commonly used figuratively, as in cluttering a page with technical details, where unnecessary elements obscure the main point.

ja: clutter：多すぎる物・情報が空間を占め、利用や理解を妨げる散らかり。
mess：物理的な散らかり・汚れ・混乱・失敗した状況を広く表す。
disorder：配置・制度・状態などに秩序がないこと。より形式的。
untidiness：物が整理・整頓されていない状態。
junk：価値がない、または不要と判断された物・情報。
debris：破壊・事故・自然現象などで残された破片・残骸。
congestion：人・車・物・情報が集中し、流れが妨げられている状態。
clutter up：物を置きすぎて場所をふさぐ・散らかす。clutter より口語的。
en: clutter is an excessive collection of objects or information that obstructs use or understanding.
mess broadly describes physical untidiness, dirt, confusion, or a badly handled situation.
disorder is a more formal word for the absence of proper arrangement, organization, or control.
untidiness is the state of not being neatly organized or arranged.
junk consists of objects or information regarded as useless or unwanted.
debris consists of fragments or remains left by destruction, an accident, or a natural event.
congestion is overcrowding that obstructs the movement of people, vehicles, objects, or information.
clutter up conversationally means filling and obstructing a place with too many things.

etymology.ja: clutter は中英語 clotter「凝固する、塊になる」などと関係すると考えられているが、詳細な語源には不確かな点がある。物が塊となって集まり、もつれたり混雑したりするという発想から、騒がしい混乱や物の集積を表すようになった。その後、部屋・机などをふさぐ乱雑な物の集まりという現在の中心的意味が確立し、さらに画面・文書・思考を複雑にする過剰な情報にも使われるようになった。
etymology.en: Clutter is generally associated with Middle English forms such as clotter, to coagulate or form into a mass, although details of its deeper origin remain uncertain. From the idea of things gathering into a tangled or crowded mass, it developed senses relating to noisy confusion and accumulated objects. Its central modern meaning became an untidy collection obstructing a room or surface, and it later extended to excessive information complicating screens, documents, and thought.

note.ja: 乱雑な物だけでなく、汚れた場所、混乱した状況、失敗なども表す一般的な語。
note.en: A general word covering untidy objects, dirty places, confused situations, and failures.

note.ja: 物・組織・社会などが適切に整理・統制されていない状態を表す。
note.en: A state in which objects, an organization, or a society lack proper arrangement or control.

note.ja: 部屋・机・外見などがきちんと整理されていないこと。
note.en: The condition of a room, desk, or appearance not being neatly arranged.

note.ja: さまざまな物・考えが順序なく混ざり合った状態やその集まり。
note.en: A confused mixture of different objects or ideas lacking order.

note.ja: 人・車・情報などが過度に集中し、通常の流れや処理が妨げられる状態。
note.en: Overcrowding of people, vehicles, or information that obstructs normal movement or processing.

We spent the afternoon clearing clutter from the spare room. — 私たちは午後を使って、空き部屋の不要な物を片付けた。
Too many icons clutter the screen and make the application difficult to use. — アイコンが多すぎて画面がごちゃごちゃし、アプリケーションが使いにくくなっている。
The report contains useful information, but unnecessary details clutter its main argument. — その報告書には有用な情報が含まれているが、不要な細部が主張の本筋を分かりにくくしている。
A patent claim should not be cluttered with limitations that add no meaningful distinction over the prior art. — 特許請求項には、先行技術に対する意味のある相違をもたらさない限定を、むやみに詰め込むべきではない。

The report contains useful information, but unnecessary details clutter its main argument.

usage.transitive: With an object, declutter means removing unnecessary items or elements from a particular place or system.
usage.intransitive: Without an object, it means engaging generally in the activity of sorting and removing clutter.
usage.physical: It commonly refers to organizing a home, room, desk, wardrobe, or storage area.
usage.digital: It can refer to deleting, organizing, or simplifying files, email, applications, screens, and interfaces.
usage.figurative: Declutter one’s mind or life means reducing unnecessary commitments, distractions, or mental burdens.
usage.result: Decluttering involves deciding what is unnecessary, not merely moving every item into a neater arrangement.

ja: 部屋・机・収納などから不要な物を取り除いて整理する
多数の所有物を選別し、処分・譲渡・移動する
画面・文書・デザインから余分な要素を除いて簡潔にする
不要なファイル・メール・アプリなどを整理・削除する
比喩的に、予定・思考・生活から余計な負担や雑念を減らす
en: to remove unnecessary objects from a room, desk, or storage area and organize the remaining space
to sort through possessions and discard, donate, or relocate unwanted items
to simplify a screen, document, or design by removing excessive elements
to organize or delete unnecessary files, email, applications, or other digital material
figuratively, to reduce unnecessary commitments, thoughts, or distractions in one’s life

nuance.ja: declutter は、単に掃除して汚れを落とす clean や、物を整然と並べ直す tidy とは異なり、不要な物・情報・要素を選別して減らすことを中心とする。declutter the room は、物を収納し直すだけでなく、不要品を捨てる・譲るなどして空間を取り戻すことを示唆する。デジタル分野では、古いファイルや不要な通知を削除すること、デザインでは画面上の情報量を減らして見やすくすることを表す。declutter your mind は比喩的な表現で、雑念や過剰な予定を減らし、集中しやすい状態にすることを意味する。
nuance.en: Declutter differs from clean, which primarily concerns removing dirt, and tidy, which concerns arranging things neatly. Its central idea is reducing the quantity of unnecessary objects, information, or elements. To declutter a room suggests not merely putting everything into orderly storage but also discarding, donating, or relocating unwanted possessions to recover usable space. In digital contexts, it includes deleting old files and unnecessary notifications. In design, it means reducing visual or informational density. Declutter your mind is figurative and refers to reducing distracting thoughts or excessive commitments to improve clarity and concentration.

ja: declutter：不要な物・情報・要素を取り除き、空間・画面・生活を簡潔にする。
tidy：物を正しい場所に置き、見た目を整然とさせる。
clean：汚れ・ほこり・細菌などを取り除いて清潔にする。
organize：物・情報・予定などを一定の体系・順序に整える。
sort out：物や問題を分類・整理し、混乱を解消する。
clear out：場所の中にある物を大幅に、または全部取り除く。
streamline：不要な段階・要素を除き、工程・組織・設計を効率化する。
clutter：多すぎる物・情報によって空間をふさぎ、利用・理解を妨げる。
en: declutter means removing unnecessary objects or information to simplify a space, screen, or life.
tidy means putting things in their proper places and making an area look orderly.
clean means removing dirt, dust, stains, or harmful material.
organize means arranging objects, information, or activities according to a system or order.
sort out means classifying and arranging things or resolving a confused problem.
clear out means removing many or all of the contents from a place.
streamline means removing unnecessary stages or elements to make a process, organization, or design more efficient.
clutter means filling a space with excessive objects or information that obstruct use or understanding.

etymology.ja: declutter は、除去・逆転を表す接頭辞 de- と clutter「散らかった物、物でふさぐ」から作られた比較的新しい語である。de- はラテン語系の接頭辞で、deactivate、declassify などと同様に、ある状態を取り除く働きを持つ。したがって declutter は文字どおりには「clutter の状態を取り除く」を意味する。住居整理やミニマリズムへの関心とともに一般化し、後にデジタル環境・デザイン・生活全般の簡素化にも用いられるようになった。
etymology.en: Declutter was formed relatively recently from the removal or reversal prefix de- and clutter, an untidy collection or the act of overcrowding a space. The Latinate prefix de- removes an existing condition, as it does in deactivate and declassify. Declutter therefore literally means removing the state of clutter. It became increasingly common in discussions of household organization and minimalism and subsequently extended to digital environments, design, work processes, and personal life.

note.ja: 物を適切な場所に置き直して整然とさせるが、必ずしも物の総量を減らすとは限らない。
note.en: To arrange objects neatly in their proper places without necessarily reducing their total quantity.

note.ja: 物・情報・活動を、利用しやすい一定の体系や順序に配置する。
note.en: To arrange objects, information, or activities into a useful system or order.

note.ja: 部屋・棚・容器などから、多くの物またはすべての物を取り除く。
note.en: To remove many or all objects from a room, shelf, container, or other space.

note.ja: 不要な複雑さ・要素を減らし、理解・実行しやすくする。
note.en: To reduce unnecessary complexity or elements and make something easier to understand or use.

note.ja: 不要な段階・作業・要素を取り除き、仕組みやデザインを効率化する。
note.en: To remove unnecessary stages, work, or elements and make a system or design more efficient.

usage.intransitive: Pile up commonly means accumulating or increasing: The work is piling up.
usage.transitive: It can mean placing objects in a pile: They piled up the boxes or piled the boxes up.
usage.separation: A pronoun object normally goes between the verb and particle: pile them up, not pile up them.
usage.abstract: Work, debt, costs, complaints, evidence, and pressure can figuratively pile up.
usage.noun: The hyphenated noun pile-up commonly means a collision involving several vehicles or, more generally, a large accumulation.
usage.register: The phrasal verb is natural in conversation and ordinary writing; accumulate is a more formal alternative.

ja: 物が積み重なり、大きな山・集積になる
物を一か所に重ねて積み上げる
仕事・書類・注文などが処理されず次々にたまる
借金・費用・損失・問題などが増え続ける
証拠・苦情・圧力などが次第に大量になる
名詞 pile-up の形で、複数車両が関係する玉突き事故
en: for objects, to accumulate into a large pile or mass
to place and stack objects on top of one another
for work, documents, or orders, to accumulate faster than they are processed
for debt, costs, losses, or problems, to continue increasing
for evidence, complaints, or pressure, to become increasingly abundant
in the noun pile-up, a collision involving multiple vehicles

nuance.ja: pile up は、個々の物・仕事・問題などが次々に加わり、目立つ量になることを表す。物理的には Boxes were piled up by the door. のように物が積み重なった状態を、比喩的には Work is piling up. のように未処理の仕事が増えている状態を表す。accumulate より口語的で、しばしば処理の遅れ・圧迫感・管理不能の兆候を含む。ただし、薪や箱を意図的に積み上げる場合には否定的意味はない。ハイフンを付けた名詞 pile-up は特に玉突き事故を意味するので、動詞 pile up と綴りを区別する必要がある。
nuance.en: Pile up describes individual objects, tasks, or problems being added until they form a noticeable quantity. Physically, Boxes were piled up by the door describes stacked objects. Figuratively, Work is piling up means that unfinished work is accumulating. It is more conversational than accumulate and often suggests delay, pressure, or an emerging loss of control. There is no necessary negative implication when someone intentionally piles up firewood or boxes. The hyphenated noun pile-up particularly denotes a multiple-vehicle collision and should be distinguished in spelling from the verb pile up.

ja: pile up：物を積み上げる、または仕事・借金・問題などが次々にたまる。
accumulate：物・金銭・情報などが時間をかけて蓄積する。より中立的・形式的。
stack up：物を整えて積み重ねる。または仕事・問題がたまる。
mount up：費用・借金・圧力・問題などが次第に増える。
build up：物質・圧力・感情・在庫などが徐々に増加する。
heap up：物を乱雑な山状に積み上げる。
back up：処理の遅れにより、交通・注文・データなどが滞留する。
pile-up：複数の車両が次々に衝突する玉突き事故。ハイフン付きの名詞。
en: pile up means stacking objects or allowing work, debt, or problems to accumulate.
accumulate neutrally and formally describes objects, money, or information gradually increasing over time.
stack up means arranging objects in a neat pile or, figuratively, allowing work or problems to accumulate.
mount up describes costs, debts, pressure, or problems gradually increasing.
build up describes a gradual increase in material, pressure, emotion, or stock.
heap up means placing objects together in a relatively disorderly mound.
back up means becoming congested or delayed because processing or movement is obstructed.
a pile-up is a hyphenated noun for a collision involving multiple vehicles.

etymology.ja: pile は中英語を経てラテン語 pila「柱、石の塊、積み重ね」に関係する語から入った。もともと物を重ねた山や集積を表し、動詞として「積み上げる」という意味を持つようになった。up は句動詞で、上方向への動きだけでなく、動作の進行・完了・量の増加を強調する。したがって pile up は、物が上へ積み重なることから、仕事・費用・問題などが大量に蓄積する比喩的意味へ広がった。
etymology.en: Pile entered English through Middle English from a word related to Latin pila, a pillar or mass. It came to denote a heap or collection of objects and then developed the verbal meaning of stacking. In phrasal verbs, up can indicate upward movement as well as increasing quantity or completion. Pile up therefore developed naturally from objects being stacked upward to the figurative accumulation of work, costs, evidence, and problems.

note.en: To accumulate material, emotion, pressure, or inventory gradually until it becomes substantial.

note.ja: 長い時間をかけて、多量の富・情報・証拠・物品などを集める。
note.en: To gather a large quantity of wealth, information, evidence, or objects over time.
