usage.intransitive: Without an object, tidy up means putting things in order generally: I need to tidy up.
usage.separation: With a noun object, both tidy up the room and tidy the room up are possible. A pronoun normally goes in the middle: tidy it up.
usage.physical: It most commonly means returning objects to their proper places and making a room or surface neat.
usage.figurative: It can mean making wording, design, data, or arrangements neater and more consistent.
usage.cleaning: Tidying up primarily concerns order and arrangement; it does not necessarily include washing or removing dirt.
usage.regionality: Tidy up is especially common in British English. Clean up and straighten up are frequently used in American English, depending on the intended action.

ja: 散らかった物を元の場所へ戻して部屋・机などを整頓する
物をきちんと並べ、場所を見た目に整った状態にする
活動・食事・催しの後に使用した物を片付ける
服装・髪などを整え、きちんとした外見にする
文書・デザイン・データなどの細部を整理し、一貫した状態にする
en: to put scattered objects back in their proper places and make a room or surface neat
to arrange things so that a place looks orderly
to put away items used during an activity, meal, or event
to make one’s clothes, hair, or general appearance neat
to organize and improve the consistency of a document, design, or set of data

nuance.ja: tidy up は、汚れを落とすことより、散らかった物を片付けて秩序を回復することに焦点を置く。tidy up the kitchen は食器や調理器具を片付けることを含むが、床や流しを洗剤で洗うところまで意味するとは限らない。clean up は汚れ・ごみを除去する意味が強く、declutter は不要品そのものを減らすことを強調する。tidy up は、物を捨てなくても、所定の場所へ戻して整然とさせれば成立する。文書について tidy up the wording と言えば、表記・構成・細かな不統一を整えることであり、大幅な書き直しとは限らない。
nuance.en: Tidy up focuses on restoring order by putting scattered things into their proper places rather than on removing dirt. Tidying up the kitchen may include putting away dishes and utensils but does not necessarily mean washing every surface. Clean up emphasizes removing dirt, rubbish, or contamination, while declutter emphasizes reducing the total quantity of unnecessary possessions. A place can therefore be tidied up without anything being discarded. To tidy up wording or a document means correcting presentation, organization, or minor inconsistencies rather than necessarily rewriting the substance.

ja: tidy up：散らかった物を適切な場所へ戻し、空間・文書などを整然とさせる。
tidy：物・場所を整頓する。tidy up とほぼ同義だが、up が完了を強調する。
clean up：汚れ・ごみ・混乱などを取り除き、清潔・正常な状態にする。
declutter：不要な物・情報を選別して減らし、空間や画面を簡潔にする。
straighten up：物の位置を直して、場所や外見を手早く整える。
put away：使用した物を収納場所・所定の位置へ戻す。
organize：物・情報・活動を一定の体系・順序に整える。
clear up：物を片付ける、問題を解決する、天候が回復するなど、文脈により意味が変わる。
en: tidy up means putting scattered things in their proper places and making a space or document orderly.
tidy has nearly the same meaning, while up emphasizes completion.
clean up means removing dirt, rubbish, contamination, or disorder.
declutter means selecting and removing unnecessary objects or information to simplify a space or screen.
straighten up means quickly correcting the position of things or making a place or appearance neat.
put away means returning something after use to its storage place or proper position.
organize means arranging objects, information, or activities according to a useful system.
clear up may mean tidying, resolving a problem, or improving weather, depending on context.

etymology.ja: tidy は中英語 tidi に由来し、もとは「時宜にかなった、適切な、良好な」という意味を持っていた。これは time と関係する古英語 tīd「時、季節」にさかのぼる。そこから「状態が良い」「きちんと整った」という意味が発達した。up は句動詞において、動作を最後まで行って望ましい状態にする完了的な働きを持つため、tidy up は「片付けを完了して整然とさせる」を意味する。
etymology.en: Tidy comes from Middle English tidi, which originally meant timely, appropriate, or in good condition. It is ultimately related to Old English tīd, time or season, the source of tide in some of its older senses. The meaning developed from suitable and satisfactory to neat and orderly. In phrasal verbs, up often marks completion or achievement of a resulting state, so tidy up emphasizes bringing the process of arranging things to a satisfactory end.

note.ja: 散らかった物の位置を直し、部屋・机・服装などを手早く整える。
note.en: To quickly correct the position of scattered objects and make a room, desk, or appearance neat.

note.ja: 物・情報・手続きなどを、適切で理解しやすい順序・状態に整える。
note.en: To arrange objects, information, or procedures into a proper and understandable order.

note.ja: 物・情報・活動を分類し、一定の体系に従って利用しやすく配置する。
note.en: To classify and arrange objects, information, or activities into an accessible system.

note.ja: 物の配置・外見を整えて、きれいで整然とした状態にする。
note.en: To improve the arrangement or appearance of something and make it neat.

note.ja: ごみ・汚れ・不要物を取り除いて、場所を清潔で整った状態にする。
note.en: To remove rubbish, dirt, or unwanted material and leave a place clean and orderly.

usage.intransitive: Without an object, clean up means to remove dirt or disorder: We need to clean up.
usage.separable: With a noun object, both clean up the room and clean the room up are possible.
usage.pronoun: A pronoun must normally come between the verb and particle: clean it up, not clean up it.
usage.broader_scope: Unlike tidy up, clean up can include washing, removing dirt, repairing environmental damage, or eliminating undesirable activity.
usage.figurative: It can mean improving a system, correcting disorganized material, or removing crime, corruption, and other problems.
usage.profit: Informally, clean up can mean making a large profit or winning a large amount of money.
usage.noun_spelling: The verb is written as two words, clean up. The noun and attributive form are usually written as one word: a cleanup or cleanup costs.

ja: 場所や物から汚れ・ごみを取り除いてきれいにする
使用後や行事の後に、散らかった場所を片付ける
汚染物質・廃棄物などを除去し、環境を回復させる
文章・データ・組織などから誤りや不要な要素を取り除く
犯罪・汚職・不正などを一掃する
口語で、多額の利益・賞金などを得る
en: to remove dirt, rubbish, or unwanted material from a place or object
to restore order after an activity, event, or another person
to remove pollutants or waste and restore an environment
to eliminate errors or unnecessary elements from a document, dataset, or organization
to eliminate crime, corruption, or other undesirable conduct
informally, to make a large profit or win a large amount of money

nuance.ja: clean up は、単に物を整然と並べるだけでなく、汚れ・ごみ・有害物質・誤り・不正など、望ましくないものを取り除いて状態を改善することを表す。tidy up は主として散らかった物を整理して見た目を整えるのに対し、clean up は拭く・洗う・廃棄するなどの実際の清掃を含みやすい。したがって、部屋を tidy up しても汚れていることはあり、clean up にはより徹底的な改善が含まれ得る。比喩的には、データの誤りを修正する、組織から汚職をなくす、文章を読みやすくするといった場合にも使われる。clean up one’s act は、自分の態度・生活・仕事ぶりを改めるという慣用表現である。
nuance.en: Clean up means improving a condition by removing something undesirable, such as dirt, rubbish, pollution, errors, or corruption. Tidy up primarily concerns arranging scattered items and making a place look orderly, whereas clean up more readily includes actual cleaning activities such as wiping, washing, and disposing of waste. A room can therefore be tidy but still unclean. Figuratively, the expression can describe correcting data, improving writing, or eliminating misconduct from an organization. Clean up one’s act is an idiom meaning to improve one’s behavior, lifestyle, or performance.

ja: clean up：汚れ・ごみ・誤り・不正などを取り除き、状態を改善する。
tidy up：散らかった物を整理し、場所や外観を整然とさせる。
clean：物や場所から汚れを取り除くことを直接表す。
clear up：散乱物・問題・誤解などを取り除き、状態を明瞭にする。
declutter：不要な所有物や情報を減らし、空間・構成を簡素にする。
sanitize：衛生上有害な微生物を減らす、または情報から機密部分を除く。
remediate：汚染・欠陥・法令違反などを是正する、専門的・形式的な語。
clean up one’s act：態度・生活習慣・仕事ぶりを改める慣用表現。
en: clean up means removing dirt, waste, errors, or misconduct in order to improve a condition.
tidy up means arranging scattered things so that a place or appearance becomes orderly.
clean directly means removing dirt from an object or place.
clear up means removing disorder, resolving a problem, or eliminating confusion.
declutter means reducing unnecessary possessions or information to create a simpler space or structure.
sanitize means reducing harmful microorganisms or removing sensitive information from material.
remediate is a technical or formal verb for correcting pollution, defects, or noncompliance.
clean up one’s act means improving one’s behavior, habits, or performance.

etymology.ja: clean は古英語 clǣne「清潔な、純粋な、汚れのない」に由来する。形容詞から「きれいにする」という動詞の用法が発達し、方向・完了を表す副詞的要素 up と結び付いて clean up となった。ここで up は必ずしも上方向を示すのではなく、行為を十分に行って完了させる意味を加える。物理的な清掃から、汚染・犯罪・誤りなどを除去する比喩的意味へ用法が広がった。名詞 cleanup は、この句動詞から形成された。
etymology.en: Clean derives from Old English clæne, meaning pure, clear, or free from dirt. The adjective developed a verbal use meaning to make clean and combined with up, which here adds a sense of thoroughness or completion rather than upward direction. The physical meaning of removing dirt broadened metaphorically to eliminating pollution, crime, corruption, and errors. The noun cleanup was subsequently formed from the phrasal verb.

note.ja: 散らかった物を適切な場所へ戻し、見た目を整然とさせる。
note.en: To put scattered things in their proper places and make an area look orderly.

note.ja: 不要な物を片付けるほか、問題・誤解・不明点を解消する。
note.en: To remove unwanted objects or resolve a problem, misunderstanding, or uncertainty.

note.ja: 不要な物・情報を選別して減らし、空間や構成を簡潔にする。
note.en: To remove unnecessary possessions or information and make a space or structure simpler.

note.ja: 衛生的な状態にする、または文書・データから機密情報などを除く。
note.en: To make something hygienic or remove sensitive or objectionable material from data or documents.

note.ja: 環境汚染・技術的欠陥・法令違反などを是正する形式的な語。
note.en: A formal term for correcting environmental contamination, technical defects, or noncompliance.

grammar.transitivity: transitive or intransitive as a verb

usage.adjective: As an adjective, tidy describes something arranged neatly and without unnecessary disorder.
usage.verb: As a verb, tidy means arranging things properly and removing visible disorder.
usage.spelling: Before endings beginning with a vowel, final y changes to i: tidier, tidiest, tidied, and tidies. It remains y in tidying.
usage.cleanliness: Tidy primarily concerns order and arrangement; something can be tidy without being completely clean.
usage.amount: Especially in British English, a tidy sum, profit, or amount means a fairly large or satisfactory one.
usage.approval: In some chiefly British informal uses, tidy can express general approval, although this sense is regional.
usage.phrasal_verb: Tidy up is often more natural than tidy alone when referring to completing a general act of putting things in order.

ja: 物が適切な場所に置かれ、散らかっていない
人の服装・外見などがきちんとしている
文章・仕事・構成などがよく整理され、扱いやすい
動詞として、物を整理して場所を整然とさせる
特にイギリス英語で、金額・利益などがかなり大きい
解決策・取り決めなどが簡潔で都合よくまとまっている
en: arranged properly and free from visible disorder
for a person’s clothing or appearance, neat and well presented
for writing, work, or a structure, clearly and conveniently organized
as a verb, to arrange things and make a place orderly
especially in British English, fairly large or substantial in amount or profit
for a solution or arrangement, conveniently simple and well organized

nuance.ja: tidy の中心は清潔さそのものではなく、物が適切な場所に収まり、外見上の乱れがないことである。したがって、机の上を整理して tidy にしても、表面にほこりが残っていれば clean とは限らない。形容詞として a tidy room、動詞として tidy the room の両方に使えるが、日常会話で「片付ける」と言う場合には tidy up の方が自然なことも多い。文章・データ・設計について使うと、構成が整い、不要な複雑さが少ないことを表す。ただし、複雑な問題に a tidy solution を与えることが、重要な例外や曖昧さを無視することを示唆する場合もある。イギリス英語の a tidy sum は「整った金額」ではなく「かなりの金額」を意味する。
nuance.en: The central idea of tidy is order rather than cleanliness itself. A desk may be tidy because everything is properly arranged while still not being clean if its surface is dusty. Tidy can be an adjective, as in a tidy room, or a verb, as in tidy the room, although tidy up is often more natural for a general act of putting things in order. Applied to writing, data, or design, it suggests a well-organized structure with little unnecessary complexity. A tidy solution can be complimentary, but it may also imply that a complicated problem has been made deceptively simple by overlooking exceptions. In British English, a tidy sum means a substantial amount of money.

ja: tidy：物が適切に配置され、散らかっていない。または物を整理する。
tidy up：散らかった物を片付け、場所を整然とさせる。
clean：汚れ・ほこり・ごみなどがなく清潔な、またはそれらを除去する。
neat：外見・配置・仕事などが整っていて、きちんとしている。

en: tidy means neatly arranged and free from disorder, or to arrange things properly.
tidy up means putting scattered things away and making a place orderly.
clean means free from dirt, dust, or rubbish, or removing such material.
neat describes an appearance, arrangement, or piece of work that is carefully ordered.
orderly means arranged or conducted according to a clear system or established order.
organized means systematically arranging information, objects, or activities.
declutter means removing unnecessary possessions or information to simplify a space or structure.
untidy means disordered or not properly arranged in appearance, work, or surroundings.

etymology.ja: tidy は、中英語で「時宜にかなった、適切な、状態のよい」を意味した形容詞に由来し、古く「時・季節」を意味した tide と関係する。そこから「満足できる、立派な」、さらに「よく整えられた、きちんとした」という現在の意味が発達した。その後、形容詞から「物を整然とさせる」という動詞の用法も生まれた。現代英語の tide は主に潮の満ち引きを表すが、古くは時や季節を表す広い意味を持っていた。
etymology.en: Tidy comes from a Middle English adjective meaning timely, suitable, or in good condition and is historically related to tide in its older sense of time or season. Its meaning developed from suitable or satisfactory to respectable and well arranged, producing the modern sense neat and orderly. The verb meaning to put things in order was subsequently formed from the adjective. Although modern tide mainly refers to the rise and fall of the sea, it formerly had the broader meaning time or season.

note.ja: 外見・配置・筆跡・仕事などが注意深く整えられ、乱れがないことを表す。

note.en: Describes things arranged or proceeding according to a clear order, system, or discipline.

note.en: Describes objects, information, or activities systematically arranged for efficient use.

note.ja: 建物・庭・外見などが継続的に手入れされ、良好な状態に保たれている。
note.en: Describes a building, garden, or appearance regularly maintained in good condition.

note.ja: 不要な物や要素が少なく、すっきりとして見やすい。
note.en: Describes a space or design containing few unnecessary objects or elements.

usage.physical_order: Untidy commonly describes a place or collection of objects that is not arranged neatly.
usage.appearance: It can describe hair, clothing, or a person’s general appearance as disordered or insufficiently neat.
usage.cleanliness: Untidy concerns arrangement and appearance rather than hygiene; an untidy place is not necessarily dirty.
usage.abstract_use: It can describe an argument, arrangement, solution, or situation that lacks a clear and orderly structure.
usage.evaluation: The word is usually mildly critical but is less forceful than chaotic, filthy, or disorganized.
usage.spelling: The final y changes to i before comparative and related endings: untidier, untidiest, untidily, and untidiness.

for a room or desk, containing scattered or disorganized objects

for handwriting, documents, or work, disorderly and difficult to follow

nuance.ja: untidy は tidy の反対で、物の配置・外見・構成に乱れがあることを表す。必ずしも dirty「汚れている」と同じではなく、清潔ではあっても物が散乱していれば untidy といえる。messy と非常に近いが、untidy は比較的穏やかで、一定の基準から見てきちんと整っていないという評価に重点がある。messy は、より目立つ混乱や、液体・食べ物などによる汚れを含むこともある。比喩的には an untidy argument や an untidy compromise のように、論理・制度・取り決めが明確に整理されず、例外や未解決の問題を残していることを表せる。
nuance.en: Untidy is the opposite of tidy and describes disorder in arrangement, appearance, or structure. It is not identical to dirty: a place can be clean but untidy if its contents are scattered. Untidy is close to messy but is generally milder and focuses on failure to meet an expected standard of neatness. Messy can suggest more conspicuous disorder or actual dirt involving food, liquid, or other material. Figuratively, expressions such as an untidy argument or an untidy compromise describe reasoning, rules, or arrangements that lack a clear structure and leave exceptions or unresolved problems.

ja: untidy：物・外見・構成がきちんと整理されておらず、乱れている。

tidy means properly arranged and orderly in appearance or structure.

etymology.ja: untidy は、否定を表す接頭辞 un- と tidy から成る。tidy は中英語で「時宜にかなった、適切な、状態のよい」ことを表し、古い意味で「時・季節」を表した tide と関係する。その意味が「良好な状態の」から「きちんと整えられた」へ発達した後、untidy はその反対である「整っていない、乱雑な」を表すようになった。untidiness と untidily も同じ構造から作られている。
etymology.en: Untidy is formed from the negative prefix un- and tidy. Tidy developed from a Middle English word meaning timely, suitable, or in good condition and is historically related to tide in its older sense of time or season. After tidy acquired the meaning neatly arranged, untidy came to express its opposite: disordered or insufficiently neat. Untidiness and untidily are later formations from the same adjective.

grammar.countability: normally uncountable

usage.uncountable: Productivity is normally uncountable: improve productivity, not improve a productivity.
usage.measurement: In economics and business, productivity generally expresses output in relation to an input such as labor, time, or capital.
usage.personal_use: In everyday workplace language, it can mean how much useful work a person completes within a particular period.
usage.output_distinction: High output does not necessarily mean high productivity if achieving it requires disproportionately large inputs.
usage.efficiency_distinction: Efficiency emphasizes avoiding wasted resources, whereas productivity emphasizes the amount of output obtained from the resources used.
usage.profit_distinction: Productivity is not the same as profitability; a productive operation can remain unprofitable because of prices, costs, or market conditions.
usage.plural: The plural productivities may be used in specialized comparisons of different industries, sectors, or production factors but is uncommon in general English.

ja: 投入した時間・労働・資本などに対して得られる生産量・成果の程度
労働者・企業・経済などが効率よく財・サービスを生み出す能力
一定時間内に完了できる有用な仕事の量
仕事・学習などを効果的に進め、成果を上げる度合い
土地・設備・システムなどが産出物を生み出す能力
経済学で、産出量を労働時間などの投入量で割って表す生産性
en: the amount of output or achievement obtained from inputs such as time, labor, or capital
the ability of a worker, company, or economy to produce goods or services effectively
the amount of useful work completed within a particular period
the degree to which work or study is conducted effectively and produces results
the capacity of land, equipment, or a system to generate output
in economics, a measure calculated by relating output to an input such as hours worked

nuance.ja: productivity は、単なる生産量ではなく、時間・労働・資本などの投入に対してどれだけの成果を得たかという関係を表す。生産量が増えても、それ以上に労働時間や費用が増えていれば、生産性が向上したとは限らない。日常的な職場の会話では、個人が一定時間にどれだけ有用な仕事を終えられるかという比較的緩やかな意味でも使われる。efficiency は無駄の少なさに、productivity は投入当たりの成果に重点がある。また profitability は収益性であり、価格・費用・需要にも左右されるため、生産性とは別の概念である。休憩や業務の整理は一時的に作業時間を減らしても、集中力を回復させて長期的な productivity を高めることがある。
nuance.en: Productivity concerns the relationship between results and the time, labor, capital, or other resources used to obtain them, rather than output alone. An increase in production does not necessarily represent higher productivity if labor hours or costs rise even more. In everyday workplace discussion, the word is also used more loosely for the amount of useful work a person completes within a given period. Efficiency emphasizes minimizing waste, whereas productivity emphasizes output per unit of input. Profitability is a separate concept affected by prices, costs, and demand. A break or organizational task may temporarily reduce working time while improving concentration and long-term productivity.

ja: productivity：時間・労働・資本などの投入に対して得られる成果・生産量の程度。
production：財・サービスを生み出す行為・過程、またはその総生産量。
output：人・機械・組織などが実際に生み出した製品・仕事・情報の量。
efficiency：時間・費用・エネルギーなどの無駄を抑えて成果を得る能力。
performance：人・機械・組織が実際に示した働きぶり・成果の総合的評価。
effectiveness：意図した目的・結果をどの程度達成できたか。
profitability：事業・製品・投資が利益を生み出す能力。
productiveness：成果を生み出す性質を表すが、productivity より使用頻度が低い。
en: productivity is the amount of output or achievement obtained in relation to time, labor, capital, or other inputs.
production is the act or process of creating goods or services, or the total amount produced.
output is the amount of goods, work, or information actually produced by a person, machine, or organization.
efficiency is the ability to obtain results while minimizing wasted time, money, or energy.
performance is a broad assessment of how well a person, machine, or organization operates.
effectiveness is the degree to which an intended objective or result is achieved.
profitability is the ability of a business, product, or investment to generate profit.
productiveness describes the quality of producing useful results but is less common than productivity.

etymology.ja: productivity は productive「生産的な」に、性質・状態を表す接尾辞 -ity を加えて作られた。productive は後期ラテン語 productivus「生み出すのに適した」に由来し、その基礎にはラテン語 producere「前へ導く、生み出す」がある。producere は pro-「前へ」と ducere「導く」から成る。当初は物を生み出す能力を広く表したが、産業化と経済分析の発展に伴い、投入量に対する産出量を示す経済的・統計的概念として定着した。
etymology.en: Productivity was formed from productive with the suffix -ity, which indicates a quality or condition. Productive derives from Late Latin productivus, meaning capable of producing, and is ultimately based on Latin producere, to lead forward or bring forth. Producere consists of pro-, forward, and ducere, to lead. The word initially referred broadly to the capacity to produce, but with industrialization and the development of economic analysis, productivity became established as a statistical relationship between output and input.

note.ja: 無駄な時間・費用・労力をできるだけ減らして成果を得る能力。
note.en: The ability to obtain results while using as little unnecessary time, money, or effort as possible.

note.ja: 一定期間に人・機械・企業などが実際に生み出した物・仕事の量。
note.en: The quantity of goods or work actually produced by a person, machine, or company during a period.

note.ja: 人・組織・設備などが職務や機能をどの程度よく果たしているか。
note.en: A broad measure of how well a person, organization, or piece of equipment performs its function.

note.ja: 採用した方法や行動が、意図した目的を実際に達成する程度。
note.en: The degree to which a method or action actually achieves its intended objective.

note.ja: 有用な結果を生み出す性質を表すが、通常は productivity の方が自然。
note.en: The quality of producing useful results, although productivity is normally the more natural term.

grammar.countability: countable
patterns: an equation of the form + expression
substitute a value into an equation

usage.mathematics: In mathematics, an equation states that two expressions or quantities are equal, normally using the equals sign.
usage.countability: Equation is countable: an equation, several equations, or a system of equations.
usage.formula_distinction: An equation asserts equality, whereas a formula commonly provides a rule for calculating a quantity or expresses a standard relationship.
usage.expression_distinction: A mathematical expression contains numbers, variables, and operations but does not necessarily assert equality.
usage.figurative: Figuratively, equation can mean a situation considered as a combination of interacting factors.
usage.equate_distinction: Equation is the noun for a mathematical statement or balanced relationship; equate is the corresponding verb.
usage.pronunciation: The middle consonant is commonly pronounced /ʒ/, as in the middle of vision.

ja: 二つの数式・数量が等しいことを等号で示す方程式・等式
未知数を含み、その値を求めることのできる数学的な式
物理量や変数の関係を表す数式
複数の要因が相互に影響する状況・関係
二つの物事を同一または同等として扱うこと
判断や計画において考慮すべき要素の組み合わせ
en: a mathematical statement that two expressions or quantities are equal
a mathematical statement containing an unknown value that can be determined
a statement expressing the relationship between physical quantities or variables
a situation involving several interacting factors
the treatment of two things as identical or equivalent
a combination of elements that must be considered in a decision or plan

nuance.ja: 数学における equation は、等号によって左右の式が等しいと主張するものである。例えば x + 2 = 5 は equation だが、x + 2 だけなら expression「数式・式」であり、等式ではない。formula は特定の値を計算する規則や一般的関係を表すことが多く、equation と重なる場合はあるものの完全な同義語ではない。日常語では、複雑な問題を構成する要因の組み合わせを表し、Money is only one part of the equation. のように使う。また、the equation of A with B のような形式的用法では、異なる二つのものを同一視することを表すが、通常の会話では equating A with B の方が自然である。
nuance.en: In mathematics, an equation asserts that the expressions on its two sides are equal, normally through an equals sign. For example, x + 2 = 5 is an equation, whereas x + 2 by itself is an expression. A formula commonly provides a rule for calculating a value or states a general relationship, so it can overlap with equation but is not an exact synonym. In everyday language, equation refers to the combination of factors making up a complicated situation, as in Money is only one part of the equation. The formal expression the equation of A with B can mean treating two things as identical, although equating A with B is more natural in ordinary usage.

ja: equation：二つの数式・数量が等しいことを示す等式、または複数要因から成る関係。
formula：値を計算する規則、または一般的な関係を記号で表した公式。
expression：数・変数・演算記号から成る式で、等号を含む必要はない。
identity：変数の許されるすべての値について成立する等式。
inequality：二つの値の大小関係を不等号で示す不等式。
calculation：数値や記号を操作して結果を求める計算過程。
variable：方程式の中で変化し得る値、または未知の値を表す記号。
equate：二つの物を等しいものとして扱う、または両者が等しいとする。
en: an equation states that two mathematical expressions or quantities are equal or represents a relationship among several factors.
a formula is a symbolic rule for calculating a value or expressing a general relationship.
an expression consists of numbers, variables, and operations and need not contain an equals sign.
an identity is an equation true for every permitted value of its variables.
an inequality states the relative size of two values by using an inequality sign.
a calculation is the process of manipulating numbers or symbols to obtain a result.
a variable is a symbol representing a value that can change or remain unknown.
equate means treating two things as equal or stating that they have the same value.

etymology.ja: equation はラテン語 aequatio「等しくすること、均等化」に由来し、フランス語を経て英語に入った。aequatio は動詞 aequare「等しくする」から作られ、その基礎には aequus「等しい、平らな、公平な」がある。英語では当初、物事を等しくする行為や状態を広く表したが、やがて数学において二つの量が等しいことを示す式を指す専門用語となった。equal、equality、equate、equivalent も同じラテン語系統に属する。
etymology.en: Equation comes through French from Latin aequatio, meaning an equalizing or making equal. Aequatio was formed from aequare, to make equal, based on aequus, meaning equal, level, or fair. In English, the word initially referred broadly to the act or condition of making things equal and later became the mathematical term for a statement that two quantities are equal. Equal, equality, equate, and equivalent belong to the same Latin word family.

note.ja: 数量を求める方法や、変数間の一般的な関係を記号で表したもの。
note.en: A symbolic rule showing how to calculate a quantity or representing a general relationship among variables.

note.ja: 数学では二つの量が等しいという関係を表し、一般語では同等性を意味する。
note.en: In mathematics, the relationship of two quantities having the same value; generally, the state of being equal.

note.ja: 二つ以上の数量・要素・事象が相互にどのように関連するかを表す一般語。
note.en: A general term for the way in which two or more quantities, elements, or events are connected.

note.ja: 数・変数・演算記号を組み合わせた数学的な式で、必ずしも等式ではない。
note.en: A mathematical combination of numbers, variables, and operations that does not necessarily assert equality.

note.ja: 複数の要素・力・利益などが釣り合っている状態を表す。
note.en: A state in which different elements, forces, or interests are appropriately proportioned.

ja: a mathematical equation — 数学上の方程式
a simple equation — 単純な方程式
a complex equation — 複雑な方程式
a linear equation — 一次方程式
a quadratic equation — 二次方程式
solve an equation — 方程式を解く
formulate an equation — 方程式を立てる
derive an equation — 方程式を導出する
substitute a value into an equation — 方程式に値を代入する
both sides of the equation — 等式の両辺
part of the equation — 状況を構成する一要素
factor something into the equation — ある要素を考慮に入れる
en: a mathematical equation
a simple equation
a complex equation
a linear equation
a quadratic equation
solve an equation
formulate an equation
derive an equation
substitute a value into an equation
both sides of the equation
part of the equation
factor something into the equation

ja: Can you solve this equation without using a calculator? — 計算機を使わずに、この方程式を解けますか。
The equation describes the relationship between pressure and temperature. — その方程式は圧力と温度の関係を表している。
Substitute the measured value for x in the equation. — 方程式の x に測定値を代入してください。
Salary is important, but flexibility is also part of the equation. — 給与は重要だが、柔軟性も考慮すべき要素の一つである。
If a patent claim defines a parameter by an equation, the symbols and method of measurement should be explained clearly in the specification. — 特許請求項がパラメータを方程式によって定義する場合、その記号と測定方法を明細書で明確に説明することが望ましい。
en: Can you solve this equation without using a calculator?
The equation describes the relationship between pressure and temperature.
Substitute the measured value for x in the equation.
Salary is important, but flexibility is also part of the equation.
If a patent claim defines a parameter by an equation, the symbols and method of measurement should be explained clearly in the specification.

grammar.countability: countable
patterns: throw in something as a freebie

usage.countability: Freebie is countable: a freebie or several freebies.
usage.meaning: It normally refers to a product, service, ticket, sample, or benefit received without direct payment.
usage.register: The word is informal; complimentary item, promotional item, or item provided free of charge is preferable in formal writing.
usage.promotion: Freebies are often distributed for advertising, customer acquisition, publicity, or goodwill.
usage.conditions: Calling something a freebie describes the absence of a direct charge but does not guarantee that it comes without conditions, data collection, or future costs.
usage.evaluation: The word can be neutral or approving, but it may sound mildly critical when suggesting that someone expects undeserved benefits.
usage.spelling: The standard plural changes final -y to -ies: freebies.

ja: 料金を支払わずにもらえる物・サービス
販売促進のために配布される無料の商品・試供品
商品や契約に追加して無料で提供される特典
企業・主催者などから無償で与えられる入場券・飲食物・贈答品
通常なら対価が必要だが、特別に無料で得られるもの
ときに、労力や資格なしに得られる利益・便宜
en: an item or service received without payment
a free product or sample distributed for promotional purposes
an additional benefit supplied at no extra charge with a purchase or agreement
a ticket, meal, gift, or other item provided free by a company or organizer
something normally requiring payment that is obtained free on a particular occasion
sometimes, a benefit or advantage obtained without effort or entitlement

nuance.ja: freebie は、「無料でもらえる物・サービス」を親しみやすく表す口語語である。企業が配る試供品、イベントの記念品、購入時のおまけ、無料チケットなどに広く使える。free gift と近いが、freebie の方がくだけており、物だけでなくサービスや便宜も含み得る。文脈によっては、単にうれしい無料特典を表す一方、He is always looking for freebies. のように、ただでもらえる物ばかり求めているという批判的な響きにもなる。また、金銭的に無料でも、個人情報の提供・自動更新・別商品の購入などの条件が付く場合があるため、freebie は必ずしも無条件の贈与を意味しない。
nuance.en: Freebie is a friendly informal term for something supplied without direct payment. It can refer to promotional samples, event merchandise, an extra item included with a purchase, a free ticket, or even a service or privilege. It overlaps with free gift but is more conversational and is not limited to physical objects. The word can express appreciation for a welcome benefit, but in He is always looking for freebies it can criticize someone for constantly seeking unearned advantages. A freebie may also require personal information, automatic renewal, or another purchase, so the term does not necessarily mean that the offer has no conditions.

ja: freebie：直接の料金を支払わずにもらえる物・サービスを表す口語語。
free gift：購入・参加などに伴って無料で与えられる贈り物。
giveaway：宣伝のために無料配布される物、または景品企画。
free sample：購入前に試してもらうため少量を無料提供する試供品。
complimentary item：企業・施設などが厚意またはサービスとして無料提供する物。
perk：仕事・会員資格などに付随する追加的な恩恵・特典。
bonus：通常の内容に追加される報酬・利益・特典。
handout：無料で配られる物や資料。文脈によっては施しという否定的な含みを持つ。
en: a freebie is an informal term for an item or service received without direct payment.
a free gift is a present supplied without additional charge, often with a purchase or participation.
a giveaway is an item distributed for promotional purposes or an event in which prizes are offered.
a free sample is a small quantity supplied without charge so that consumers can try a product.
a complimentary item is something formally provided free by a business, facility, or host.
a perk is an additional benefit associated with employment, membership, or a particular position.
a bonus is an extra reward, benefit, or feature added to what is normally provided.
a handout is freely distributed material or assistance and can sometimes imply charity or dependency.

etymology.ja: freebie は free「無料の、自由な」を基礎に、親しみや軽い響きを与える語尾 -bie を加えて作られた口語語である。freeby という綴りも歴史的に見られるが、現在の標準的な綴りは freebie である。20世紀に、無料で提供される商品・サービス・便宜を表す語として広く使われるようになった。語尾 -bie 自体が一定の意味を持つ生産的な接尾辞というより、くだけた名詞らしい形を作る要素と考えられる。
etymology.en: Freebie is an informal formation based on free with the playful noun ending -bie. The spelling freeby has also appeared historically, but freebie is now standard. During the twentieth century, the word became widely used for goods, services, and privileges supplied without direct payment. The element -bie is better understood as giving the word a casual noun-like form than as a regularly productive suffix with a precise independent meaning.

note.ja: 宣伝・販促のために無料で配布される物、または無料景品を提供する企画。
note.en: An item distributed free for advertising or a promotion in which free prizes are offered.

note.ja: 購入・契約・イベント参加などに伴って、追加料金なしで与えられる贈り物。
note.en: A gift supplied without additional charge, often in connection with a purchase, agreement, or event.

note.ja: 企業・ホテル・主催者などがサービスまたは厚意として無料提供する物。
note.en: An item supplied free of charge by a business, hotel, organizer, or host as a service or courtesy.

note.ja: 職務・地位・会員資格などに付随して得られる追加的な利益・優遇。
note.en: An additional benefit or privilege associated with a job, position, or membership.

note.ja: 通常得られる内容に加えて提供される追加の報酬・利益・機能。
note.en: An extra reward, benefit, or feature supplied in addition to what is normally received.

ja: get a freebie — 無料の品をもらう
receive a freebie — 無料特典を受け取る
offer freebies — 無料の品を提供する
give away freebies — 無料の品を配る
hand out freebies — 無料サンプルなどを配布する
a promotional freebie — 販売促進用の無料品
a corporate freebie — 企業から提供される無料品・接待
a useful freebie — 役に立つ無料品
a freebie from a company — 企業からもらった無料品
include something as a freebie — 何かを無料のおまけとして含める
throw in a freebie — 無料のおまけを追加する
look for freebies — 無料でもらえる物を探す
en: get a freebie
receive a freebie
offer freebies
give away freebies
hand out freebies
a promotional freebie
a corporate freebie
a useful freebie
a freebie from a company
include something as a freebie
throw in a freebie
look for freebies

ja: The café gave us a freebie with our first order. — そのカフェは、初回の注文に無料のおまけを付けてくれた。
Visitors received several freebies at the trade show. — 来場者は展示会でいくつかの無料配布品を受け取った。
The basic app is free, but some of its apparent freebies require a paid subscription. — そのアプリの基本版は無料だが、無料特典に見える機能の一部には有料契約が必要である。
The company handed out promotional freebies bearing its new logo. — その会社は、新しいロゴを付した販促用の無料品を配布した。
Before distributing branded freebies, the company asked its trademark counsel to check whether the proposed mark was available for use. — ブランド名を付した無料配布品を配る前に、その会社は使用予定の商標を使用できるか商標担当の弁理士に確認を求めた。
en: The café gave us a freebie with our first order.
Visitors received several freebies at the trade show.
The basic app is free, but some of its apparent freebies require a paid subscription.
The company handed out promotional freebies bearing its new logo.
Before distributing branded freebies, the company asked its trademark counsel to check whether the proposed mark was available for use.

grammar.countability: countable
patterns: a physical / concrete embodiment of + idea

usage.personification: In general English, the embodiment of a quality is a person or thing that represents that quality in a particularly clear or complete form.
usage.physical_form: Embodiment can mean a concrete or physical form in which an abstract idea, design, or principle is expressed.
usage.patent_use: In patent writing, an embodiment is a particular way of implementing or realizing an invention.
usage.actuality: A patent embodiment need not necessarily be a prototype that was actually constructed or tested; the context should distinguish working examples from predicted or hypothetical examples.
usage.claim_scope: A disclosed embodiment is not automatically identical to the full scope of a claim, and limitations of a particular embodiment should not be inserted into broader claim language without an appropriate interpretive basis.
usage.number: Patent specifications commonly describe multiple embodiments, alternatives, and variations.
usage.register: The word is formal in its general sense and highly conventional in patent and technical writing.

ja: 抽象的な性質・思想などを明確に体現する人・物
考え・原理・設計などが具体的または物理的な形を取ったもの
ある概念を目に見える形で表現したもの
特許・技術文書で、発明を具体的に実現する一つの構成・実施形態
発明の特定の構造・手順・材料・条件などを組み合わせた態様
複数の選択肢のうち、説明または図示された一つの具体例
en: a person or thing that clearly and completely represents an abstract quality or idea
a concrete or physical form taken by an idea, principle, or design
a visible or tangible expression of a concept
in patent and technical writing, a particular implementation or realization of an invention
a particular combination of structures, steps, materials, or conditions implementing an invention
one specific example among several possible alternatives described or illustrated

nuance.ja: 一般英語の embodiment は、抽象的な性質が人や物に具体的に現れていることを表す。She is the embodiment of patience. と言えば、その人が忍耐という性質を典型的かつ完全に表しているという強い表現になる。特許実務では「実施形態」と訳され、発明を実現する具体的な構造・方法・条件などを指す。ただし、embodiment は必ずしも実際に製作された試作品を意味せず、明細書上の説明として構成された態様も含み得る。また、一つの実施形態に記載された細部が当然に請求項の限定となるわけではない。請求項の範囲、明細書全体、明示的な定義や限定などを踏まえて判断する必要がある。preferred embodiment は「好ましい実施形態」であって、唯一の実施形態を意味しない。
nuance.en: In general English, embodiment describes an abstract quality or idea taking a particularly clear form in a person or thing. She is the embodiment of patience strongly suggests that she represents patience in an exemplary or nearly complete way. In patent practice, embodiment refers to a particular structure, method, condition, or other way of realizing an invention. It does not necessarily mean that a physical prototype was actually built; an embodiment may be presented descriptively or predictively in the specification. Nor does every detail of one embodiment automatically become a limitation of a broader claim. Claim scope must be assessed from the claim language, the specification as a whole, and any relevant definitions or disclaimers. A preferred embodiment is a favored implementation, not necessarily the only possible one.

ja: embodiment：性質・思想を具体的に体現するもの、または発明の具体的な実施形態。
example：一般的な説明を具体化するために挙げられる個別の例。
implementation：設計・計画・技術を実際に機能する形へ移すこと、またはその実現形態。
realization：考え・計画・設計などを現実のものにすること、またはその結果。
manifestation：性質・状態・現象などが外部に現れたもの。
personification：抽象的な性質を人として表すこと、またはその性質を典型的に示す人。
prototype：試験・評価・開発のために製作された初期的な実物モデル。
claim：特許で保護を求める発明を文言によって画定する部分。実施形態とは同一ではない。
en: an embodiment is a concrete representation of a quality or idea or a particular implementation of an invention.
an example is a particular case used to illustrate a general explanation.
an implementation is the act or result of putting a design, plan, or technology into working form.
a realization is the process or result of making an idea, plan, or design real.
a manifestation is an outward appearance or expression of a quality, condition, or phenomenon.
personification is representing an abstract quality as a person or a person who characteristically displays it.
a prototype is an early physical model constructed for testing, evaluation, or development.
a claim defines in words the invention for which patent protection is sought and is not identical to an embodiment.

etymology.ja: embodiment は動詞 embody に、行為・状態・結果を表す接尾辞 -ment を加えて作られた。embody は em-「中に入れる、ある状態にする」と body「身体、形あるもの」から成り、文字どおりには「身体を与える、形あるものにする」という発想を持つ。body は古英語 bodig に由来する。抽象的な思想・性質を具体的な形で表すという意味から、技術や発明を特定の構造・方法として具体化した「実施形態」という専門的用法が発達した。
etymology.en: Embodiment was formed from the verb embody with the suffix -ment, which denotes an act, condition, or result. Embody combines em-, meaning to put into or cause to be in a particular state, with body, a physical form. Body derives from Old English bodig. The literal idea is therefore giving a body or concrete form to something. From the representation of an abstract idea or quality in tangible form developed the technical use for a particular structure or method in which an invention is realized.

note.ja: 抽象的な性質・概念を人の姿で表すこと、またはその性質を典型的に示す人物。
note.en: The representation of an abstract quality as a person or a person who characteristically represents that quality.

note.ja: 内在する性質・状態・現象などが、観察できる形で外部に現れたもの。
note.en: An observable outward appearance or expression of an underlying quality, condition, or phenomenon.

note.ja: 思想・計画・設計などを具体化して現実のものにすること、またはその結果。
note.en: The act or result of making an idea, plan, or design concrete and real.

note.ja: 計画・設計・技術を、実際に使用または機能できる形で実現すること。
note.en: The act or result of putting a plan, design, or technology into usable or functioning form.

note.ja: 一般的な概念・型・設計を、特定の具体例として実現することを表す技術的な語。
note.en: A technical term for creating a specific concrete instance of a general concept, type, or design.

ja: the embodiment of courage — 勇気の体現
the embodiment of elegance — 優雅さを体現するもの
a physical embodiment of an idea — 思想を物理的に具体化したもの
a concrete embodiment of a principle — 原理の具体的な表現
an embodiment of the invention — 発明の一実施形態
in one embodiment — 一実施形態では
in another embodiment — 別の実施形態では
according to an embodiment — 一実施形態によれば
a preferred embodiment — 好ましい実施形態
an alternative embodiment — 代替的な実施形態
the illustrated embodiment — 図示された実施形態
the disclosed embodiments — 開示された実施形態
en: the embodiment of courage
the embodiment of elegance
a physical embodiment of an idea
a concrete embodiment of a principle
an embodiment of the invention
in one embodiment
in another embodiment
according to an embodiment
a preferred embodiment
an alternative embodiment
the illustrated embodiment

ja: She was widely regarded as the embodiment of patience and kindness. — 彼女は忍耐と親切を体現する人物として広く認められていた。
The building is a physical embodiment of the architect’s philosophy. — その建物は建築家の思想を物理的な形で体現したものである。
This prototype is the first practical embodiment of the original concept. — この試作品は、当初の構想を初めて実用的な形にしたものである。
In one embodiment, the sensor is mounted inside the housing. — 一実施形態では、センサーは筐体の内部に取り付けられる。

The claim should not necessarily be limited to the dimensions shown in the preferred embodiment unless the claim language or specification provides an appropriate basis for that limitation. — 請求項の文言または明細書にその限定の適切な根拠がない限り、請求項を好ましい実施形態に示された寸法へ当然に限定すべきとは限らない。
en: She was widely regarded as the embodiment of patience and kindness.
The building is a physical embodiment of the architect’s philosophy.
This prototype is the first practical embodiment of the original concept.
In one embodiment, the sensor is mounted inside the housing.
The claim should not necessarily be limited to the dimensions shown in the preferred embodiment unless the claim language or specification provides an appropriate basis for that limitation.

grammar.countability: countable; sometimes used in the plural for a set of technical requirements
patterns: the specification discloses / describes + subject matter

usage.requirements: A specification commonly states detailed requirements that a product, system, material, or service must satisfy.
usage.plural: Specifications or the informal specs often refers to a list of technical characteristics such as size, capacity, speed, and performance.
usage.document: The word can refer either to an individual requirement or to the document containing a collection of requirements.
usage.patent_use: In patent practice, specification refers to the written disclosure associated with a patent application, but its precise scope and relationship to the description, claims, abstract, and drawings depend on the jurisdiction and context.
usage.claim_distinction: A patent specification explains the invention, while the claims define the subject matter for which protection is sought; the two should not be treated as interchangeable.
usage.contract_use: In a contract or procurement context, specifications may establish binding technical or performance requirements.
usage.abbreviation: Spec and specs are common in engineering and informal business communication but may be unsuitable for formal legal drafting.

ja: 製品・材料・システムなどが満たすべき詳細な要件・仕様
寸法・性能・品質・構成などを具体的に定めた仕様書
契約・発注などで求められる技術的または機能的条件
何かを正確かつ具体的に特定・記述すること
特許出願において発明を説明・開示する明細書またはその構成部分
製品の性能・容量・形式などを列挙した諸元
en: a detailed requirement that a product, material, or system must satisfy
a document defining dimensions, performance, quality, construction, or other characteristics
a technical or functional condition required under a contract or purchase order
the act or result of identifying or describing something precisely
in patent practice, the written disclosure describing an invention or a formally defined part of the application
a listed technical characteristic such as the capacity, performance, or format of a product

nuance.ja: 一般的な specification は、製品・システム・業務などが満たすべき要件を詳細に定めたものを指す。単数形は個別の要件または仕様書全体のいずれにも使われ、複数形 specifications は寸法・性能・容量などの諸元一式を表すことが多い。requirements は必要条件を広く表すのに対し、specifications は通常、より具体的で測定・検証可能な技術的条件を示す。特許分野では一般に「明細書」と訳されるが、specification が含む範囲は法域や手続によって異なり、description と常に完全な同義語になるわけではない。また、明細書に記載された実施形態と、claims によって画定される保護対象も区別する必要がある。
nuance.en: In general use, a specification sets out detailed requirements for a product, system, or task. The singular can refer to either one particular requirement or an entire specification document, while specifications often means a collection of technical characteristics such as dimensions, capacity, and performance. Requirements is broader, whereas specifications usually suggests more concrete and verifiable technical conditions. In patent practice, specification is commonly translated into Japanese as meisaisho, but the parts included within the term vary by jurisdiction and procedure, and specification is not always completely synonymous with description. The embodiments disclosed in a specification must also be distinguished from the protected subject matter defined by the claims.

ja: specification：製品・システムなどの詳細な要件・仕様、または特許の明細書。
requirement：製品・行為・制度などが満たさなければならない必要条件。
standard：品質・性能・手続などを統一的に評価するための基準。
description：物・発明・出来事などの性質や構成を言葉で説明したもの。
instruction：何をどのように行うべきかを示す指示・使用説明。

en: a specification is a detailed technical requirement or document, or a patent specification describing an invention.
a requirement is a condition that a product, action, or system must satisfy.
a standard is an established basis for consistently assessing quality, performance, or procedure.
a description is a verbal account of the nature, structure, or characteristics of something.
an instruction tells someone what to do or how to perform an action.
a criterion is an individual condition used as a basis for judgment, assessment, or selection.
a claim defines in words the invention for which patent protection is sought.
spec is an informal shortened form of specification, especially common in the plural specs.

etymology.ja: specification は、ラテン語 specificare「具体的に示す、特定する」に由来する。specificare は species「種類、外観」と facere「作る」から構成され、ある物を特定の種類・形として明確にするという発想を持つ。英語では、物事を具体的に特定する行為から、製品や作業に求められる詳細を列挙した文書という意味が発達した。さらに、発明の内容を具体的に開示する特許文書を表す専門用語として定着した。specify、specific、specimen、species も歴史的に関連する語である。
etymology.en: Specification derives from Latin specificare, meaning to identify or describe particularly. Specificare was formed from species, meaning kind or appearance, and facere, to make. The underlying idea was to make something definite as a particular kind or form. In English, the act of identifying something precisely developed into the sense of a document listing the details required of a product or task. The word also became established as a technical term for the patent document disclosing an invention. Specify, specific, specimen, and species belong to the same historical word family.

grammar.countability: normally uncountable in the state-of-uncertainty sense; countable for a limbo dance or particular theological conception
grammar.transitivity: not applicable as a noun; intransitive as a dance verb
patterns: leave / keep someone or something in limbo
exist in a state of limbo

usage.fixed_phrase: In the figurative sense, limbo is most commonly used in the fixed phrase in limbo.
usage.article: Do not normally say in a limbo for general uncertainty; use in limbo or in a state of limbo.
usage.figurative: It describes an unresolved intermediate state in which progress, status, or future action remains uncertain.
usage.theology: Capitalized Limbo can refer to a traditional theological conception of a state or place at the border of hell for certain souls.
usage.dance: The limbo is a West Indian dance or contest in which participants bend backward and pass beneath a progressively lowered bar.
usage.register: The figurative expression is natural in conversation, journalism, administration, business, and legal discussion.

ja: 決定・承認・結果などを待ち、先へ進めない宙ぶらりんの状態
法的・行政的な地位が確定していない中間状態
計画・申請・交渉などが中断され、将来が不明な状態
伝統的なカトリック神学で、天国にも地獄の刑罰にも属さないとされた辺境的な状態・場所
上体を後ろへ反らし、次第に低くなる棒の下を通る西インド諸島のダンス・競技
en: an unresolved state in which a decision, approval, or result is awaited and no progress can be made
an intermediate condition in which legal or administrative status remains uncertain
a suspended situation in which the future of a plan, application, or negotiation is unclear
in traditional Catholic theology, a proposed border state or place for certain souls excluded from heaven but not subjected to the punishment of the damned
a West Indian dance or contest involving bending backward to pass beneath a progressively lowered bar

nuance.ja: 日常的な in limbo は、単に待っているだけでなく、必要な決定・承認・情報が得られないため、地位も今後の行動も確定できない状態を表す。The project is in limbo. なら、正式に中止されたわけではないが、再開・実行できる見通しも立っていないという意味になる。on hold は意図的・一時的な中断を表すのに対し、in limbo は誰が決めるのか、いつ解決するのかさえ不明な不安定さを強調する。神学上の Limbo と、棒の下をくぐるダンスの limbo は意味だけでなく語源も別と考えられているため、カード内で区別する必要がある。
nuance.en: Figurative in limbo means more than simply waiting. It suggests that a necessary decision, approval, or piece of information is unavailable, leaving both present status and future action unresolved. The project is in limbo means that it has not formally been canceled but also has no clear route toward resumption or implementation. On hold often describes a deliberate temporary pause, whereas in limbo emphasizes instability and uncertainty about who will decide the matter or when it will be resolved. The theological Limbo and the dance called the limbo are generally treated as distinct not only in meaning but also in etymological development.

ja: in limbo：決定・地位・将来が確定せず、先へ進めない宙ぶらりんの状態で。
on hold：計画・処理などが意図的かつ一時的に保留されて。
pending：決定・処理・結果を待っている。行政・法律文脈で一般的。
in abeyance：権利・計画・活動などが一時停止・休止状態にある。形式的。
up in the air：計画・結果などが未定で、どうなるか分からない。口語的。
at a standstill：活動・交渉・交通などが完全に停止して。
deadlock：当事者が譲歩せず、交渉・意思決定が進まない行き詰まり。
the limbo：上体を後ろへ反らして低い棒の下を通るダンス・競技。
en: in limbo means being unable to proceed because status, a decision, or the future remains unresolved.
on hold means deliberately and temporarily paused.
pending means awaiting a decision, process, or result and is common in administrative and legal contexts.
in abeyance formally describes a right, plan, or activity temporarily suspended.
up in the air informally means undecided or uncertain.
at a standstill means that activity, negotiation, or movement has stopped completely.
a deadlock is a situation in which negotiation or decision-making cannot proceed because neither side will yield.
the limbo is a dance or contest involving bending backward beneath a low horizontal bar.

etymology.ja: 宙ぶらりんの状態を表す limbo は、中世ラテン語の句 in limbo「辺境・縁において」に由来し、その基礎であるラテン語 limbus は「縁、境界」を意味した。神学上、天国と地獄の刑罰のいずれにも明確に属さない境界的な場所・状態を表したことから、決定不能な中間状態という比喩的意味が生じた。一方、ダンス名の limbo は西インド諸島英語に由来し、limber「柔軟な」との関係が指摘されているが、詳細な成立過程には不確かな点がある。
etymology.en: Limbo in the sense of an uncertain state comes from the Medieval Latin phrase in limbo, at the border, based on Latin limbus, edge or boundary. Its theological use for a state not clearly belonging either to heaven or to the place of punishment produced the figurative meaning of an unresolved intermediate condition. The dance name limbo has a separate West Indian English history and has been associated with limber, flexible, although details of its formation remain uncertain.

note.ja: 事実・結果・将来などが明らかでなく、確信を持てない状態を広く表す。
note.en: A broad term for a state in which facts, outcomes, or future developments are not known with confidence.

note.ja: 活動・権利・処理などが一時的に停止されている状態。
note.en: A temporary stopping of an activity, right, process, or operation.

note.ja: 権利・決定・活動などが一時的に効力を停止し、待機状態にあること。
note.en: A formal term for a right, decision, or activity being temporarily inactive or awaiting resolution.

note.ja: 双方が相手を動かせず、交渉・争いなどが進展しなくなった状態。
note.en: A situation in which opposing sides cannot make progress or force the other side to move.

note.ja: 比喩的に、不快で長く続き、解放を待つ苦しい中間状態。limbo より苦痛を強調する。
note.en: Figuratively, an unpleasant prolonged intermediate state of waiting, emphasizing suffering more strongly than limbo.

usage.meaning: The expression is a literary or humorous way of saying that someone is asleep.
usage.grammar: It normally follows a form of be or another verb describing entry into or continuation of sleep.
usage.plural: The established expression uses the plural arms, not the singular arm.
usage.capitalization: Morpheus is a proper name and must begin with a capital letter.
usage.register: The phrase is rare, elevated, and deliberately figurative; asleep, sleeping, or fast asleep is more natural in ordinary conversation.
usage.tone: It may create a poetic tone or humorously make an ordinary act of sleeping sound grand.
usage.mythology: The expression alludes to Morpheus, a dream-forming figure in Ovid who is conventionally described as a god of dreams.

ja: 眠っている、眠りについている
深い眠りに包まれている
夢の世界に入っている
詩的または文学的に、眠りの神に抱かれている
普通の睡眠を大げさかつユーモラスに表現した状態
en: asleep or in the state of sleeping
enveloped in deep or peaceful sleep
within the world of dreams
poetically, held in the embrace of the god of dreams
humorously, engaged in the ordinary act of sleeping

nuance.ja: in the arms of Morpheus は asleep を神話的な比喩で表した、かなり文学的な慣用句である。眠りを、Morpheus という存在の腕に優しく抱かれている状態として描くため、安らかな眠り・深い眠りという印象を伴いやすい。ただし、必ずしも睡眠の質を客観的に示す表現ではない。現代の日常会話で使うと、単に asleep と言えば済むところを古風に飾っているため、気取った冗談として聞こえることが多い。通常は be in the arms of Morpheus と状態を表し、fall または sink into the arms of Morpheus とすれば眠りに落ちる動きを表す。定型形は複数形の arms であり、Morpheus は固有名詞なので大文字で始める。
nuance.en: In the arms of Morpheus is a distinctly literary idiom that replaces the ordinary word asleep with a mythological image. It portrays sleep as being gently held in the embrace of Morpheus and therefore often suggests peaceful or deep sleep, although it does not objectively describe sleep quality. In present-day conversation, the phrase can sound humorously grand or deliberately old-fashioned because asleep would normally be sufficient. Be in the arms of Morpheus describes the state of sleeping, while fall or sink into the arms of Morpheus describes entering that state. The fixed expression uses the plural arms, and Morpheus is capitalized as a proper name.

ja: in the arms of Morpheus：眠っていることを神話的に表す、文学的・ユーモラスな慣用句。
asleep：眠っている状態を表す最も一般的で中立的な形容詞。
sleeping：実際に眠る行為が進行中であることを表す。

in the land of Nod：眠っていることをユーモラスまたは古風に表す慣用句。
fall asleep：起きている状態から眠っている状態へ移る。
en: in the arms of Morpheus is a literary or humorous mythological expression meaning asleep.
asleep is the most common neutral adjective for being in a state of sleep.
sleeping describes the act of sleep as being in progress.
fast asleep means completely or deeply asleep.
sound asleep means sleeping deeply enough not to be easily disturbed.
dead to the world is an informal idiom for sleeping so deeply that one is unaware of the surroundings.
in the land of Nod is a humorous or old-fashioned idiom meaning asleep.
fall asleep means changing from wakefulness to sleep.

etymology.ja: この表現は、眠っている人を Morpheus の腕に抱かれているものとして描く神話的な比喩である。Morpheus はローマの詩人オウィディウスの『変身物語』に登場し、眠りの中で人間の姿を巧みに作り出す存在として描かれる。その名はギリシャ語 morphē「形、姿」に関係し、夢の中でさまざまな人間の姿を取る能力を示唆する。後世には広く「夢の神」として知られるようになり、その腕に抱かれることが「眠る」の詩的な婉曲表現となった。
etymology.en: The expression metaphorically portrays a sleeping person as being held in the arms of Morpheus. Morpheus appears in Ovid’s Metamorphoses as a figure skilled at forming and reproducing human shapes in dreams. His name is associated with Greek morphe, meaning form or shape, alluding to his ability to assume human forms in dreams. He later became widely known as a god of dreams, and being held in his arms consequently developed into a poetic circumlocution for sleeping.

note.ja: 完全に眠っていることを表す、一般的で自然な表現。
note.en: A common and natural expression meaning completely or deeply asleep.

note.ja: 周囲の小さな物音では起きないほど深く眠っている。
note.en: Sleeping deeply enough not to be easily awakened by surrounding sounds.

note.ja: 眠りの世界にいることを、古風またはユーモラスに表す慣用句。
note.en: An old-fashioned or humorous idiom describing someone as being in the world of sleep.

note.ja: 周囲の出来事に全く気づかないほど熟睡していることを表す口語表現。
note.en: An informal expression for being so deeply asleep as to be unaware of everything nearby.

note.ja: 眠っていることを柔らかく、やや文学的に表す語。
note.en: A gentle and somewhat literary word describing someone as sleeping.

grammar.countability: usually uncountable for accommodation; countable for a protective enclosure
patterns: be mounted / accommodated in a housing

usage.accommodation: Housing is normally uncountable when it means homes or accommodation collectively: affordable housing, not affordable housings.
usage.individual_home: For one particular place where someone lives, use a house, a home, an apartment, or a housing unit rather than a housing.
usage.enclosure: In engineering, a housing is a countable outer structure that contains, supports, or protects a mechanical or electronic component.
usage.plural: The plural housings is normal for multiple casings or enclosures but not normally for multiple homes.
usage.market: Housing commonly functions attributively in expressions such as housing market, housing policy, and housing costs.
usage.pronunciation: Housing is pronounced with /z/, reflecting the verb house /haʊz/, rather than the noun house /haʊs/.
usage.patent_use: In patent claims, housing can identify a structural enclosure, but its boundaries, components, and relationship to other elements may require further clarification.

ja: 人々が居住するための住宅・住居を集合的に表す語
住宅の提供・整備・管理
特定の集団に提供される宿舎・居住施設

en: houses, apartments, and other places to live considered collectively
the provision, development, or management of places for people to live
residential accommodation provided for a particular group
the sector concerned with homes, property markets, and residential policy
a structure containing, supporting, or protecting a mechanical or electronic component
an outer case or body enclosing the internal parts of a device

nuance.ja: housing は、住宅・社会政策の文脈と、機械・特許の文脈で可算性が異なる。住宅・住居を集合的に表す場合は通常不可算で、We need more affordable housing. のように用いる。一戸の住居を a housing とは通常いわず、a house、an apartment、a home、a housing unit などを使う。一方、工学分野の a housing は、部品を収容・支持・保護する「筐体」であり、複数形 housings も自然である。housing は casing や enclosure と重なるが、必ずしも完全に密閉された構造を意味せず、装置の本体や支持構造を兼ねることもある。特許文言では、housing が一体部品なのか、複数部品から構成されるのかは、この語だけでは必ずしも確定しない。
nuance.en: Housing differs in countability between its residential and engineering senses. When it refers collectively to homes or accommodation, it is normally uncountable, as in We need more affordable housing. One residence is not normally called a housing; a house, an apartment, a home, or a housing unit is used instead. In engineering, a housing is a countable structure that contains, supports, or protects components, and the plural housings is entirely natural. Housing overlaps with casing and enclosure but does not necessarily imply a completely sealed structure and may also serve as the main body or support of a device. In patent language, housing alone does not always establish whether the structure is integral or assembled from several parts.

ja: housing：集合的な住宅・住居、または機械・装置の部品を収容する筐体。
house：独立した一戸の建物としての家、または人・物を収容する。

residence：人が居住する家・建物、または居住という状態を表す形式的な語。

en: housing means residential accommodation collectively or a structure containing and protecting parts of a machine or device.
a house is an individual residential building, while the verb house means providing space for people or objects.
a home is a place where someone lives and feels a sense of personal belonging.
accommodation is a place provided for temporary or permanent residence or lodging.
a residence is a formal term for a home, building, or the state of living in a particular place.
an enclosure is a structure surrounding and separating an object or area.
a casing is an outer cover protecting mechanical or electronic components.
a shell is a relatively thin outer structure surrounding internal parts.

etymology.ja: housing は house に、行為・結果・物を表す接尾辞 -ing が付いて成立した。house は古英語 hus「家、住居」に由来し、ドイツ語 Haus、オランダ語 huis などと同族である。名詞 house の語末は /s/ だが、「収容する」を意味する動詞 house は /z/ で発音されるため、そこから生じた housing も /ˈhaʊzɪŋ/ と発音される。「人を住まわせること・住居」という意味から、物を内部に収容する構造、すなわち機械や装置の筐体を表す意味も発達した。
etymology.en: Housing was formed from house with the suffix -ing, which can denote an action, result, or associated object. House derives from Old English hus, meaning a dwelling, and is related to German Haus and Dutch huis. The noun house ends in /s/, but the verb house, meaning to accommodate or contain, is pronounced with /z/, giving housing the pronunciation /ˈhaʊzɪŋ/. From the senses of providing people with places to live and accommodating something developed the engineering meaning of a structure that contains or protects parts of a machine or device.

note.ja: 人が滞在・居住するために提供される部屋・建物などを広く表す。
note.en: A broad term for rooms or buildings provided for people to stay or live in.

note.ja: 居住目的で使用される住宅・土地を、不動産として捉える表現。
note.en: Houses, apartments, or land considered as property intended for residential use.

note.ja: 部品・装置・空間を囲み、外部から区切る構造。
note.en: A structure that surrounds a component, device, or space and separates it from the outside.

note.ja: 装置や部品の周囲を覆い、衝撃・汚れなどから保護する外側のケース。
note.en: An outer cover placed around a device or component to protect it from impact, dirt, or other conditions.

note.ja: 機械・器具の主要な構造部分で、他の部品を支持・収容することがある。
note.en: The main structural part of a machine or instrument, which may support or contain other components.

grammar.countability: normally uncountable for unwanted or worthless material; countable for the separate ship sense
grammar.plural: junks in the ship sense; not normally used for rubbish
patterns: clear out / get rid of junk

usage.uncountable: Junk is normally uncountable when it means unwanted or worthless material: a lot of junk, not many junks.
usage.individual_item: Use a piece of junk or an item of junk for one particular unwanted object.
usage.verb: As a verb, junk means discarding, abandoning, or deciding not to use something.
usage.attributive: Before another noun, junk indicates something unwanted, unhealthy, of poor quality, or intended for discarded material.
usage.evaluation: Calling an object junk is strongly dismissive and expresses a judgment that it has little value or usefulness.
usage.technology: In computing and communication, junk can refer to unwanted email, files, data, search results, or automatically generated content.
usage.ship_homonym: A junk can also mean a traditional East or Southeast Asian sailing vessel; this is a separate countable sense with a different history.
usage.drug_slang: Junk has also been used as slang for heroin, but this sense is context-dependent and should be used with caution.

en: old, unwanted, or discarded objects and material
something regarded as having very little value or quality
unwanted files, data, or search results in a computer system
unwanted advertising, mail, or email
as a verb, to discard an object or abandon a plan
attributively, unhealthy, poor-quality, or unwanted
in a separate sense, a traditional Chinese or East Asian sailing vessel

nuance.ja: junk は、不要・無価値・低品質だと判断された物を広く表す、くだけた語である。rubbish や trash と重なるが、junk は古い機械、壊れた家具、使わないケーブルなど、場所を占めながら残されている物に特によく使われる。必ずしも完全な廃棄物ではなく、所有者には不要でも修理・再利用・収集が可能な場合がある。That computer is junk. のように可算物を直接 junk と呼べるが、文法上の junk はこの意味では通常不可算である。動詞では、物を捨てるだけでなく、計画・制度・提案などを採用せず廃止することも表す。なお、a Chinese junk の junk は伝統的な帆船を表す別義であり、「がらくた」という評価とは関係しない。
nuance.en: Junk is an informal and dismissive term for material considered unwanted, worthless, or of poor quality. It overlaps with rubbish and trash but is especially common for old machines, broken furniture, unused cables, and similar objects that remain while taking up space. Such material is not necessarily beyond all use; it may still be repaired, recycled, collected, or valuable to someone else. A countable object can be described as junk, as in That computer is junk, but junk remains grammatically uncountable in this sense. As a verb, it can mean discarding an object or abandoning a plan, policy, or proposal. The separate expression a Chinese junk refers to a traditional sailing vessel and carries no suggestion that the vessel is worthless.

ja: junk：不要・無価値・低品質だと見なされる物、またはそれを廃棄する。
rubbish：不要な廃棄物を広く表すイギリス英語の一般語。発言を「くだらない」と評する際にも使う。
trash：ごみ・廃棄物を表す主にアメリカ英語の一般語。
garbage：主に家庭から出る生ごみなどの廃棄物。比喩的に質の低い情報も表す。
clutter：必要性の低い物が集まり、空間や表示を雑然とさせている状態。
scrap：再利用・リサイクルのために残された金属・材料の断片や廃材。
debris：破壊・事故・工事などの後に残る破片・残骸。
discard：不要になった物を捨てることを中立的・やや形式的に表す。
en: junk is unwanted, worthless, or poor-quality material, or the act of discarding or abandoning something.
rubbish is the general British English term for waste and can also dismiss an idea as nonsense.
trash is the common American English term for discarded material or waste.
garbage commonly means household waste and can figuratively describe very poor-quality information.
clutter is an accumulation of unnecessary things that makes a space or display disorderly.
scrap is waste metal or other leftover material retained for reuse or recycling.
debris consists of scattered fragments or remains left by destruction, an accident, or construction.
discard is a neutral and somewhat formal verb meaning to throw away something no longer wanted.

etymology.ja: 「がらくた」を意味する junk は、中英語で古い船舶用ロープや索具を表した語に由来すると考えられている。使い古したロープは切り分けられ、再利用される低価値の材料となったため、意味が廃品・不要物全般へ広がった。そこから「価値の低い物」、さらに動詞の「廃棄する、放棄する」という用法が生じた。一方、伝統的な東アジアの帆船を表す junk は別系統の語で、ヨーロッパ諸語がマレー語・ジャワ語系の船舶名称を介して取り入れたものとされる。
etymology.en: Junk in the sense of discarded material is generally traced to a Middle English word for old ship's rope or cable. Worn rope could be cut apart and reused as low-value material, allowing the meaning to broaden to discarded or unwanted objects generally. From this developed the senses poor-quality material and, as a verb, to discard or abandon. Junk meaning a traditional East Asian sailing vessel has a separate origin and entered European languages through a Malay or Javanese term for a type of ship.

note.ja: 不要な廃棄物を広く表し、特にイギリス英語で日常的に使われる。
note.en: A broad everyday term for unwanted waste, especially common in British English.

note.ja: 捨てられる物・ごみを表す、特にアメリカ英語で一般的な語。
note.en: A common term, especially in American English, for material that is thrown away.

note.ja: 多数の不要な物が空間を占め、乱雑な状態を生じさせていることを表す。
note.en: An accumulation of unnecessary objects creating disorder in a space.

note.ja: 製造・解体などで残り、再利用やリサイクルが可能な金属・材料。
note.en: Metal or other material left from manufacturing or dismantling and potentially suitable for reuse.

note.ja: 使用後に不要となった物質・材料を広く表す、中立的で正式な語。
note.en: A broad, neutral term for material that is no longer wanted after use or production.

patterns: be called off because of + noun

usage.cancellation: Call off commonly means canceling a planned event, activity, or arrangement before it is completed.
usage.termination: It can also mean ordering an activity already in progress, such as a search, attack, or strike, to stop.
usage.separability: With a noun object, both call off the meeting and call the meeting off are possible.
usage.pronoun: A pronoun must come between the verb and particle: call it off, not call off it.
usage.agent: The subject is normally a person or organization with authority or practical ability to cancel or stop the activity.
usage.register: Call off is neutral and natural in conversation; cancel or terminate may be preferable in formal documents.
usage.legal_context: In legal or contractual writing, call off may be too informal or imprecise unless it is defined; cancel, terminate, withdraw, or discontinue may identify the intended legal effect more clearly.

ja: 予定されていた会議・試合・行事などを中止する
計画・取引・契約交渉などを取りやめる
進行中の捜索・攻撃・作戦などを打ち切る
ストライキ・抗議行動などの中止を命じる
人・動物に追跡・攻撃・批判をやめさせる
婚約・結婚式などの予定を破棄する
en: to cancel a planned meeting, game, event, or other activity
to abandon a plan, deal, or negotiation
to order an ongoing search, attack, or operation to stop
to bring a strike, protest, or similar action to an end
to order a person or animal to stop pursuing, attacking, or criticizing someone
to cancel an engagement, wedding, or similar arrangement

nuance.ja: call off は、予定されていたことを実施前に中止する場合と、すでに始まっている行動を途中で打ち切る場合の両方に使える。call off the meeting は会議を開催しないことにし、call off the search は進行中の捜索を終了させることを表し得る。postpone や put off は後日に延期するだけで再実施を予定しているのに対し、call off は原則としてその予定・活動自体を中止する。ただし、後から新たに計画し直すことまでは妨げない。契約について call off the contract と言うこともあるが、法的な効果を正確に示す必要がある文書では terminate、cancel、rescind、withdraw などを事情に応じて使い分けるべきである。
nuance.en: Call off can describe either canceling something before it begins or stopping an activity already in progress. Call off the meeting means deciding not to hold it, while call off the search may mean ending an ongoing search. Postpone and put off move an activity to a later time with an expectation that it may still occur; call off normally cancels the activity itself, although a new event can later be arranged. People sometimes say call off the contract, but legal writing should select a more precise verb such as terminate, cancel, rescind, or withdraw according to the intended legal effect.

ja: call off：予定・行事を中止する、または進行中の活動を打ち切る。
cancel：予定・予約・行事などを実施しないことにする最も一般的な語。
postpone：予定を中止せず、後の日時まで延期する。
put off：予定・決定・行動を後回しにする、より口語的な表現。
terminate：契約・雇用・活動などを正式に終了させる。
abort：開始済みの計画・任務・処理を完了前に緊急停止する。
withdraw：提案・申請・支援などを撤回する。
call for：何かを必要とする、公に要求する、または正式に募集する。
en: call off means canceling a planned event or ordering an ongoing activity to stop.
cancel is the general verb for deciding that an appointment, reservation, or event will not take place.
postpone means moving an activity to a later time rather than canceling it.
put off is a more conversational expression for delaying an event, decision, or action.
terminate means formally bringing a contract, employment relationship, or activity to an end.
abort means stopping an operation, mission, or process before completion, often because of an urgent problem.
withdraw means removing a proposal, application, offer, or support that was previously presented.
call for means requiring something, publicly demanding it, or formally inviting submissions.

etymology.ja: call は古ノルド語 kalla「大声で呼ぶ、名付ける」に由来する。off は接触・継続している状態から離れることを表す。もともと call off は、人や動物を呼び戻して追跡・攻撃などをやめさせることを表した。そこから、命令によって活動を停止させるという意味が広がり、会議・試合・計画などを「中止する」という現代の一般的用法が発達した。
etymology.en: Call derives from Old Norse kalla, meaning to cry out or name. Off expresses movement away from contact or continuation. Call off originally described recalling a person or animal and thereby stopping a pursuit or attack. From the idea of ending an activity by command developed the broader modern meaning of canceling a meeting, event, plan, or arrangement.

note.ja: 予定されていた行事・予約・注文などを実施または有効化しないことにする。
note.en: To decide that a planned event, reservation, order, or arrangement will not take place or remain effective.

note.ja: 計画・任務・技術的処理などを、完了する前に途中で停止する。
note.en: To stop a plan, mission, or technical process before it has been completed.

note.ja: 契約・雇用・活動などを、正式な効果を伴って終了させる。
note.en: To formally bring a contract, employment relationship, or continuing activity to an end.

note.ja: 計画・試み・方針などを断念し、それ以上続けない。
note.en: To give up a plan, attempt, or policy and cease pursuing it.

note.ja: 継続していた活動・サービス・手続などを終了し、以後行わない。
note.en: To stop an activity, service, or procedure that had previously been continuing.

usage.predicative: As an adjective, alike normally follows a linking verb: The two designs are alike.
usage.attributive_warning: Do not normally place alike directly before a noun; use similar, identical, or matching: similar designs, not alike designs.
usage.adverb: As an adverb, alike means in the same or a similar way: The law treats them alike.
usage.two_or_more: Alike normally compares two or more people, objects, actions, or situations.
usage.group_pairing: The pattern A and B alike means both A and B without distinction.
usage.degree: More alike and most alike are possible when comparing degrees of similarity.
usage.identity: Alike usually means similar rather than completely identical, unless strengthened by exactly or almost exactly.

ja: 二人以上の人・二つ以上の物が互いによく似ている
外見・音・性質・行動などが同じようである
副詞として、同じ方法・同じ程度で
複数の人・集団を区別せず平等に
A and B alike の形で、AもBも同様に
異なる対象が共通の特徴・影響を持つことを表す
en: similar to each other in the case of two or more people or things
having a similar appearance, sound, quality, or manner of behavior
as an adverb, in the same or a similar way
without distinction and with equal treatment of different people or groups
in the pattern A and B alike, both A and B equally
sharing a characteristic, experience, or effect despite other differences

nuance.ja: alike は、二つ以上の対象が互いに似ていることを表す。形容詞としては通常、The sisters are alike. や They look alike. のように補語として使い、名詞の直前には置かない。したがって「似た製品」は alike products ではなく similar products という。副詞では treat everyone alike「全員を同じように扱う」のように、方法・態度・影響が同じであることを表す。A and B alike は「AもBも等しく」という形式的で簡潔な表現である。alike は完全な同一性より類似性を表すのが普通であり、identical より弱い。ただし exactly alike とすれば、見分けられないほどよく似ていることを表せる。
nuance.en: Alike describes two or more subjects as similar to one another. As an adjective, it normally functions predicatively, as in The sisters are alike or They look alike, and is not ordinarily placed directly before a noun. Similar products is therefore standard, whereas alike products is not. As an adverb, it describes identical or comparable treatment, manner, or effect, as in treat everyone alike. The construction A and B alike is a concise and somewhat formal way of saying both A and B equally. Alike normally expresses similarity rather than complete identity and is therefore weaker than identical, although exactly alike can indicate an extremely close resemblance.

ja: alike：二つ以上の人・物が互いに似ている、または同じように。
like：前置詞として、ある対象が別の対象に似ていることを表す。
similar：特徴が共通しているが、完全には同一でない。名詞の前にも置ける。
identical：あらゆる重要な点で完全に同一である。
resembling：外見・性質などが別の物に似ている。
equally：程度・数量・扱いなどが等しく。
likewise：前述の内容と同じように、同様に。
unlike：人・物が互いに似ていない、または比較対象とは異なる。
en: alike means similar to each other or in the same way and normally follows a linking verb.
like functions as a preposition when one subject resembles another.
similar describes shared characteristics without complete identity and can appear before a noun.
identical means completely the same in every relevant respect.
resembling means having an appearance or quality similar to something else.
equally means to the same degree, in the same amount, or with the same treatment.
likewise means in the same way as something previously mentioned.
unlike means not similar to each other or different from the object of comparison.

etymology.ja: alike は、中英語 alike、alyke などの形に由来し、古英語の表現 on gelice「同じように」と関係する。最初の a- は、もともと「～の状態で、～の仕方で」という意味を持った要素にさかのぼり、like に相当する部分は「形・性質が同じ」という意味を表した。副詞の「同じように」という用法が早くから存在し、そこから「互いに似ている」という形容詞的用法も発達した。like、likeness、likely なども同じゲルマン語系の語族に属する。
etymology.en: Alike developed from Middle English forms such as alike and alyke and is related to the Old English expression on gelice, meaning in the same way. The initial a- ultimately reflects an element meaning in a particular state or manner, while the part corresponding to like conveyed similarity in form or nature. The adverbial meaning in the same way was established early, and the predicative adjectival meaning similar to each other subsequently developed. Like, likeness, and likely belong to the same Germanic word family.

note.ja: 重要な特徴を共有するが、完全に同一ではないことを表す最も一般的な語。
note.en: The most general word for sharing important characteristics without being completely identical.

note.ja: 外観・内容・性質などが完全に同一であることを表す。
note.en: Describes people or things as completely the same in appearance, content, or nature.

note.ja: 性質・水準・規模などが比較できるほど似ていることを表す。
note.en: Describes things sufficiently similar in quality, level, or scale to permit comparison.

note.ja: 程度・量・扱いなどに差がなく、等しいことを表す副詞。
note.en: An adverb indicating no difference in degree, amount, importance, or treatment.

note.ja: 前に述べた人・物・行動と同じように、という意味の副詞。
note.en: An adverb meaning in the same way as a person, thing, or action previously mentioned.
