a lead role is the central part in a film, play, or other production.
a lead or leash is a strap or cord attached to an animal to control its movement.

etymology.ja: 名詞 lead /liːd/ は動詞 lead「導く、率いる」から発達した。動詞は古英語 lǣdan に由来し、人・動物を前方から案内することを表した。そこから、「先頭に立つこと」が競争上の首位や組織上の主導権を表すようになった。さらに、人をある方向へ導く情報が捜査上の lead、購入へ導く接点が sales lead、物語や舞台を率いる役が the lead と呼ばれるようになった。動物用の引き綱や電気機器の接続線も、対象を導く物という発想に基づく。金属の lead /led/ は別の語源を持つ。
etymology.en: The noun lead pronounced /liːd/ developed from the verb lead, to guide or direct. The verb comes from Old English lǣdan and originally described conducting a person or animal from the front. Being at the front consequently produced the senses first position in a competition and initiative or control in an organization. Information pointing an investigation in a direction became a lead, a contact potentially leading to a purchase became a sales lead, and a role guiding a dramatic work became the lead. The animal strap and electrical connector similarly reflect the idea of conducting or guiding. The metal lead, pronounced /led/, has a separate history.

note.ja: 競争・交渉・状況において、他者より成功しやすい有利な立場。
note.en: A favorable position making success more likely in a competition, negotiation, or situation.

note.ja: 他者を待たずに行動を開始し、物事を進める力・主導権。
note.en: The ability or authority to begin action and move something forward without waiting for others.

note.en: A fact, object, or piece of information that helps solve a crime, mystery, or problem.

note.en: The central or most important role in a film, play, or stage production.

note.ja: 商品・サービスを将来購入する可能性のある人・組織。
note.en: A person or organization considered likely to purchase a product or service in the future.

grammar.countability: normally uncountable as a material; countable plural uses are rare and technical
grammar.plural: not normally used; leads may refer to different samples, forms, or compositions in specialized contexts
patterns: comply with limits on lead content

usage.pronunciation: The metal lead is pronounced /led/, unlike the verb and nonmetal noun lead, pronounced /liːd/.
usage.uncountable: As the name of a material or element, lead is normally uncountable: made of lead, not made of a lead.
usage.article: No article is normally used when referring to the substance generally: Lead is a metal.
usage.symbol: Its chemical symbol Pb derives from the Latin name plumbum.
usage.compounds: Lead commonly modifies another noun in compounds such as lead pipe, lead paint, and lead battery.
usage.pencil: Pencil lead does not normally contain metallic lead; it is chiefly made from graphite mixed with other materials.
usage.safety: Lead is toxic, so lead-containing dust, paint, water, and industrial materials require appropriate assessment and handling.
usage.figurative_adjective: Leaden can literally mean made of lead or figuratively mean heavy, slow, dull, or gloomy.

en: a soft and dense metallic element with the chemical symbol Pb and atomic number 82
a heavy metallic material used in applications such as radiation shielding, weights, and storage batteries
a metal historically used extensively in paint, pipes, solder, and numerous manufactured products
a toxic element capable of accumulating in the body and causing adverse health effects
in compounds such as lead paint and lead pipe, containing or made from lead
in pencil lead, the graphite-based writing core of a pencil, which does not normally contain metallic lead

nuance.ja: 金属の lead は /led/ と発音し、「導く」を意味する動詞や「首位・手掛かり」を意味する名詞 lead /liːd/ とは同綴異音語である。鉛は柔らかく加工しやすいうえ密度が高く、蓄電池・おもり・放射線遮蔽などに利用される。一方で毒性があり、古い塗料・配管、汚染されたほこり・土壌・水、製造工程などが曝露源になり得る。lead-free は、製品や材料が適用される基準上、鉛を含まない、または鉛含有量が規定値以下であることを示すが、具体的な許容値は法域・製品分類・規格によって異なる。なお pencil lead という名称は歴史的な誤認に由来し、現代の鉛筆の芯は通常、黒鉛を主成分とする。
nuance.en: The metal lead is pronounced /led/, making it a heteronym of lead /liːd/, the verb meaning guide and the noun meaning first position or clue. Lead is soft, workable, and dense, which has made it useful in storage batteries, weights, and radiation shielding. It is also toxic, and possible exposure sources include old paint and pipes, contaminated dust, soil or water, and industrial processes. Lead-free indicates that a product contains no lead or remains below an applicable lead-content threshold, but the precise permitted amount depends on the jurisdiction, product category, and governing standard. Pencil lead is a historical name based on an earlier misconception; a modern pencil core normally consists principally of graphite rather than metallic lead.

en: lead is the soft, dense, and toxic metallic element with the symbol Pb and atomic number 82.
heavy metal is a broad classification for relatively dense metals and does not refer exclusively to toxicity.
Pb is the chemical symbol for lead and derives from the Latin name plumbum.
lead-based means containing lead as a principal ingredient or component.
lead-free means containing no lead or no more than the amount permitted by an applicable standard.
graphite is a form of carbon and the principal material in modern pencil cores.
solder is an alloy melted to join metal components and may be lead-containing or lead-free.
leaden means made of lead, lead-colored, or figuratively heavy, slow, or gloomy.

etymology.ja: 金属名 lead は古英語 lēad に由来し、同系語は古いゲルマン諸語にも見られるが、それ以前の起源は確定していない。元素記号 Pb は英語名ではなく、ラテン語で鉛を意味する plumbum に由来する。plumber「配管工」も同じラテン語系統に属し、これはかつて配管に鉛が広く使用されたことによる。pencil lead という表現は、黒鉛がかつて鉛の一種だと誤認されていた歴史を反映する。動詞 lead「導く」は古英語 lǣdan に由来し、金属名とは別語源である。
etymology.en: The metal name lead comes from Old English lēad. Cognate forms occur in older Germanic languages, although its deeper origin is uncertain. The chemical symbol Pb derives not from the English name but from Latin plumbum, lead. Plumber belongs to the same Latin word family because lead was historically used extensively in pipes. The expression pencil lead reflects the former misconception that graphite was a kind of lead. The verb lead, to guide, derives from Old English lǣdan and has a separate etymological history.

note.ja: ラテン語 plumbum に由来する、鉛の国際的な元素記号。
note.en: The international chemical symbol for lead, derived from Latin plumbum.

note.en: A broad category of relatively dense metals that includes lead.

note.en: An explicit expression identifying metallic lead and avoiding confusion with the other senses of lead.

note.ja: 原子番号82を持つ元素として鉛を特定する科学的な表現。
note.en: A scientific designation identifying lead as the element with atomic number 82.

grammar.countability: normally uncountable as a noun
grammar.transitivity: mainly intransitive as a verb; transitive use occurs in some business and institutional contexts
patterns: a sign / measure / lack of progress

usage.uncountable: Progress is normally uncountable: We made progress, not We made a progress.
usage.unit: For an individual development, use an advance, improvement, achievement, or step forward.
usage.verb: As a verb, progress usually means develop, improve, or move forward and is generally intransitive.
usage.prepositions: Use progress in for a field, on or with for a task, and toward or towards for a goal.
usage.collocation: The standard expression is make progress, not do progress.
usage.work_in_progress: Work in progress means work that has begun but has not yet been completed.
usage.neutral_direction: Progress usually implies improvement, but the verb can neutrally describe movement through stages, including the development of a disease or problem.
usage.pronunciation: Both the noun and verb are commonly stressed on the first syllable in modern English, although some speakers give the verb stronger second-syllable stress.

ja: 目標・完成・改善へ向かって前進すること・進歩

動詞として、前進する、改善する、発展する
病気・問題・状況などが次の段階へ進む
en: movement forward toward a goal, completion, or improvement
development in skill, knowledge, performance, or circumstances
advancement of a project, task, or negotiation toward completion
development in science, technology, society, or another field
movement through time, a process, or a series of stages
as a verb, to advance, improve, or develop
for a disease, problem, or situation, to move into a further stage

nuance.ja: progress は通常不可算名詞であり、some progress、significant progress、a great deal of progress のように使う。個別の進展を数える場合は an advance、an improvement、a step forward などを用いる。make progress は、目標や完成へ近づくことを表すが、必ずしも作業全体が完了したとは意味しない。動詞では The project is progressing well. のように、自動詞として進行・改善を表す。通常は肯定的な語だが、the disease progressed や the conflict progressed のように、好ましくない物事がさらに進行する場合にも使える。progress と progression は重なるものの、progression は特に段階的な移行・順序そのものに焦点を置きやすい。
nuance.en: Progress is normally uncountable and appears in expressions such as some progress, significant progress, and a great deal of progress. To count individual developments, use an advance, an improvement, or a step forward. Make progress means moving closer to a goal or completion but does not imply that the entire task has been finished. As a verb, it is usually intransitive, as in The project is progressing well. Although progress normally has a positive evaluation, it can describe an undesirable development in the disease progressed or the conflict progressed. Progress and progression overlap, but progression more readily emphasizes an ordered or gradual movement through stages.

ja: progress：目標・改善・完成へ向かう前進・進歩、または前進すること。
advance：前方への移動、または特定分野における個別の進展・発展。
development：成長・変化・完成へ向かう継続的な発達過程。
improvement：品質・能力・状態などが以前より良くなること。
progression：一定の順序・段階を経て進むこと。
growth：数量・規模・能力・経済などが大きくなること。
achievement：努力によって達成された具体的な成果。
work in progress：開始されているが、まだ完成していない仕事・作品。
en: progress is movement toward a goal, improvement, or completion, or the act of moving forward.
an advance is forward movement or an individual improvement in a particular field.
development is a continuing process of growth, change, or movement toward completion.
improvement is a change making a quality, ability, or condition better than before.
progression is movement through an ordered sequence or series of stages.
growth is an increase in size, quantity, capacity, or economic activity.
an achievement is a specific result successfully obtained through effort.
work in progress is work that has started but has not yet been completed.

etymology.ja: progress はラテン語 progressus「前進、進行」に由来し、これは progredi「前へ進む」の過去分詞から形成された。progredi は pro-「前へ」と gradi「歩く、進む」から成る。grade、gradual、graduate、congress などにも、歩み・段階を表す同じラテン語系の要素が見られる。英語では当初、場所・過程を前方へ進むことを表し、のちに知識・社会・科学などがより良い状態へ発展するという意味が強くなった。
etymology.en: Progress derives from Latin progressus, an advance or forward movement, formed from the past participle of progredi, to move forward. Progredi combines pro-, forward, and gradi, to step or walk. Related ideas of steps and movement also appear historically in words such as grade, gradual, graduate, and congress. In English, progress initially described physical or procedural movement forward and later developed the prominent sense of improvement in knowledge, society, science, and other fields.

note.ja: 前方への動き、または科学・技術・知識などにおける具体的な進展。
note.en: Forward movement or a specific development in science, technology, knowledge, or another field.

note.ja: 成長・変化・完成へ向かい、徐々に形や能力を得る過程。
note.en: The process of gradually growing, changing, or acquiring a more complete form or capacity.

note.ja: 品質・状態・能力・成果などを、以前より良くする変化。
note.en: A change making a quality, condition, ability, or result better than it was.

note.ja: 困難がある中で、目標・解決・完成へ向かって得られた進展。
note.en: Progress made toward a goal, solution, or completion, especially despite difficulty.

note.ja: 一定の順序に従い、複数の段階を通って進行すること。
note.en: Movement through a sequence of stages in a particular order.
